**James and Becky Economou**

## IN LOVING MEMORY OF OUR PARENTS AND GRANDPARENTS

**Christ Economou and Sophia Economou**  
**Reverend Antonios Kalogeropoulos and Presvytera Katina Kalogeropoulos**[^5]

Christ Economou was born in Rendina, Greece in 1890. His grandfather, the village priest, placed him at the psaltiri (chanter’s stand) around the age of nine. Left legally blind by a high fever, Christ memorized from hearing what other chanters had learned from books. Arriving in America at age 21, he served the church in every city in which he lived, always without remuneration for himself and without reimbursement for the materials he purchased for the choir or the chanters. In 1913, Christ became the First Chanter in the “new” church of Sheboygan, Wisconsin. He went on to serve in churches in Washington State, California, Texas, and finally Tulsa, Oklahoma. In Tulsa, Christ organized a women’s choir, possibly the first women’s Greek Orthodox choir in America. Later, men joined and it became a typical four-part choir. He recruited and trained 15 other chanters during his tenure and continued as First Chanter until his death in 1973. During his 74 years of service to the church, Christ missed only two Sundays, and that was because of illness. His devotion and stewardship were recognized by Bishops and Archbishops, and he received the title of Tonsured Anagnostis.

*(Printed Page v)*

=== LEAF p8 ===

Although Christ Economou [the cantor] had no formal music training in his youth, he studied Byzantine music most of his life, and received vocal and instrumental music lessons throughout his time in America. He constantly transcribed Byzantine music into Western notation. In 1945, Christ wrote a concise version of the Typikon. The small book spelled out the important points of the services and pointed out mistakes in the original Violakis Typikon. If there were questions or differences in a section, he suggested how they could be resolved.

The study of the Typikon was a passion for my father, Christ Economou. That is why my family and I wanted to see this book published. This scholarly opus, the new bilingual Typikon, is a polychronion of effort and achievement by talented writers blessed by the Holy Spirit. I think it is fitting that the spiritual vision of a man who was physically blind should be realized in such a glorious way.

**James Economou**

*(Printed Page vi)*

=== LEAF p9 ===

# INTRODUCTION

The present work makes available to the Greek Orthodox Church in America in English translation the most authoritative guide to the order of its services, namely the *Typikon of the Great Church of Christ* by George Violakis, Head Chanter (Protopsaltis) of the Patriarchate of Constantinople at the end of the 19th century.

This treatise was composed after extensive study and deliberation by a committee consisting of four hierarchs and the Head Chanter George Violakis, which was appointed by the Holy Synod of the Patriarchate of Constantinople. It was written in its final form by Violakis himself and published in Constantinople in 1888. Thereafter, the Holy Patriarchate established the Violakis Typikon as the sole authoritative document outlining and stipulating the order (*taxis*) of all the services celebrated within the Church.

Throughout the centuries, the Church has made a continuous effort to make its services more inspiring to its worshipers, thus producing over time several Typika, each one amplifying and refining its predecessor. This sustained effort must have been inspired by St. Paul’s exhortation to us how to conduct our lives as well as how to worship God in His temple: «Πάντα δὲ εὐσχημόνως καὶ κατὰ τάξιν γινέσθω» (“Let all things be done decently and in order.”)[^6] 1 Corinthians 14:40.

It was this desire to preserve and perpetuate the order and beauty of our church services as an intrinsic, vital part of the experience of worship that impelled Dr. George T. Demos, a devoted, highly trained church musician (a medical physician by profession) to republish the Typikon by George Violakis. He wanted to reassert its sacramental authority and bring it anew to the awareness of our Church in this country by casting the book into a bilingual format, the English translation aligned with and facing the original Greek text exactly, page by opposing page. To make the work more meaningful, Dr. Demos added a dictionary of terms related to the Typikon, which he assiduously compiled and adapted from various sources.

To make the work’s contents more accessible to today’s user, Dr. Demos and I updated the complicated section where the yearly shifting Movable Feasts coincide variously with the Immovable Feasts, whose dates

*(Printed Page vii)*

=== LEAF p10 ===

have been fixed for all time. Since the original Violakis Typikon was based on the Julian Calendar, we put next to each Julian date its exactly corresponding date of the Gregorian Calendar, which is in use in the Church today. See the Chart of the Feasts (Πίναξ τοῦ Ἑορτοδρομίου), pp. 924 ff. [For the order of service as well as the hymnology (text and music) for the liturgies of the Sundays and Immovable Feasts coinciding variously with the Movable Feasts, see Theodore Bogdanos, *The Byzantine Liturgy: Hymnology and Order*, Denver, Colorado, 1993, pp. 283 ff.][^7]

The English translation was undertaken by Rev. Robert Athas, who, as both scholar and practicing liturgist, brought to this demanding task an expert, intimate knowledge of Orthodox ritual. Fr. Athas had already translated the Triodion section in the Violakis Typikon as his thesis for his Master of Divinity degree at the St. Vladimir Theological Seminary in New York. In time, I was asked by Dr. Demos to contribute to the further refinement of the translation and the work’s editorial form.

George Demos immersed himself in this project for more than 16 years. He defied physical ailments and protracted therapies — even the threat of impending sudden death — in order to finish this work for the Church. It was in the early hours of the morning that he passed away while inserting some final touches into his computer.

After his death, I proceeded to put the work into its final form as we both had conceived it. Its publication was most generously undertaken by Poti Doukas (an aerospace engineer), a gifted member of the Choir of the Assumption Cathedral in Denver, Colorado, and Dr. George Stefanidakis (a retired chemical engineer), a member of the choir and a chanter at Annunciation Cathedral in Houston, Texas. Through his computer expertise, Dr. Stefanidakis carried out several difficult corrections and updated the entire process of printing the final version. In the meantime, James Economou, a former choir director of the Church, in an extraordinary gesture of generosity, had offered to fully finance the publication of the work.

Finally, those of us who have collaborated on this project bring now this book to God as an offering, laying it like a piece of woven, multicolored tapestry at the footsteps of His throne.

**Theodore Bogdanos**

Note: Editor Dr. George Demos fell asleep in the Lord in 2012, his introduction to this book unwritten. Yet, he left behind a full acknowledgement of his indebtedness to those who contributed to the making of this book. This acknowledgement follows here:

*(Printed Page viii)*

# ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS

### By Dr. George T. Demos

A project of this size and complexity relied on the assistance of many individuals. Foremost was the immense effort of the book’s principal translator, Fr. Robert Athas,[^8] a graduate of Saint Vladimir’s Orthodox Seminary in Crestwood, New York, and former Proistamenos of the Holy Trinity Greek Orthodox Church in Tulsa, Oklahoma, of the Greek Orthodox Metropolis of Denver. Dr. Bogdanos is a Professor Emeritus of Medieval English and European (Byzantine) Literature at San Jose State University in California. God give him [Dr. Theodore Bogdanos] strength.

# GREEK ORTHODOX METROPOLIS OF DENVER

## INTRODUCTORY COMMENTARY

Mere words are most inadequate to offer a proper introduction or commentary to this massive work of the Typikon of the Great Church of Christ in both Greek and English. For one to consider the time, the labor, especially, the sacrificial love which contributed to this exceptional ministry of preserving the holy Byzantine tradition of worship and chant is to stand in awe and thanksgiving. Dr. George T. Demos of blessed memory, who worked patiently for sixteen years to achieve this publication, succeeded in surpassing any other work of its kind concerning Greek Orthodox liturgical practice.[^10]

All who acquire the use of this phenomenal accomplishment will always be grateful to those dedicated people who contributed their talent for the completion of what was most assuredly a true labor of love for the Church. It is proper to cite the Reverend Father Robert Athas of the Greek Orthodox Archdiocese, as well as Dr. Theodore Bogdanos who were both much involved with Dr. George Demos in bringing about this critical publication for the preservation of our liturgical and musical heritage.

I can never say enough about Dr. Demos, with whom I had many welcomed encounters, as he attempted to be faithful to the Typikon of the Church. In my twenty years of knowing him, never did he demonstrate any type of frustration in his holy project. His patience was a paramount sign of his deep dedication. The fact that his soul departed this life, while he was sitting at his desk in the early hours of the morning, continuing his work, is the greatest testimony to his commitment and religious fervor.

In reflection of his final hours with us for the sake of preserving our sacred way of worship, all who use this beautiful work will

offer grateful thanks to God for blessing Dr. Demos in completing this work. Countless Orthodox Christians will benefit greatly in singing praises to God which will inspire our faithful people to continue their life of worship in our ancient traditions for their sanctification.

# INTRODUCTION TO THE ENGLISH TRANSLATION

In 1985, the Denver Diocese Choir Federation held its annual conference in Tulsa, Oklahoma. I was the Proistamenos of the Holy Trinity parish there. Sitting in my office during the Conference one afternoon, chatting with some of the conferees, Dr. George Demos scanned the long wall of bookshelves. His eyes settled on a copy of the thesis I wrote for my Master of Divinity. The thesis was titled “The Triodion in the Typicon of the Great Church.”[^12] George asked if I would like to translate the rest of the Typikon. Not realizing what was involved, I agreed, and twenty years later this volume is the result.

It was not just a work of sitting down with a dictionary but a real collaboration that gave me the opportunity for wonderful conversations with Dr. Demos and with Dr. Theodore Bogdanos. Besides the work of parish and family life which would take my attention for most of the time, the hardest part of this task was remembering that we were in a four-hour difference in time zones. The easiest part was the joy of sharing our mutual love of the Typikon and our excitement in discovering footnotes to the footnotes! And comparing various Typika: Jerusalem, etc.

George Demos’ best direction to me was his insistence that “If you can make me understand it, I know we are on the right track.” I only regret that George did not live to see this work completed. I remember him with great fondness both for his humor and his humanity and his great love for the Church and for this great work of love. May his memory be eternal! Now, my hope is that this English translation of the Typikon will be helpful to all priests, choir directors, chanters and other church musicians.

The Typikon ends with the exclamation: «Τέλος καὶ τῷ Θεῷ δόξα!» (“The end and glory to God!”)[^13] It is truly God Who is the author and finisher of all things and to Him be honor and glory unto the ages of ages! Amen!

**Rev. Robert T. Athas**  
Protopresbyter  

*(Printed Page xiii)*

# GUIDE TO PHONETIC USAGE[^15]

## (ΦΩΝΗΤΙΚΟΣ ΟΔΗΓΟΣ)

### Compiled by George T. Demos, M.D.

| Greek Letter | Phonetic Equivalent & Pronunciation | Greek Letter | Phonetic Equivalent & Pronunciation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Α, α** | a as in father | **Ξ, ξ** | x as in x-ray |
| **Β, β** | v as in victory | **Ο, ο** | o as in torn |
| **Γ, γ** | g (soft) as in Greek *gamos* | **Π, π** | p as in point |
| **Δ, δ** | d (soft) as the th in then | **Ρ, ρ** | r as in rhythm (rolled as the dd in kiddy) |
| **Ε, ε** | e as in bet | **Σ, σ, ς** | s as in silk |
| **Ζ, ζ** | z as in zone | **Τ, τ** | t as in top |
| **Η, η** | i as the ee in see | **Υ, υ** | y as in party / i as the ee in see |
| **Θ, θ** | th as in thorn | **Φ, φ** | f as in father |
| **Ι, ι** | i as the ee in see | **Χ, χ** | ch (soft) as in German *Bach* |
| **Κ, κ** | k as in king | **Ψ, ψ** | ps as in perhaps |
| **Λ, λ** | l as in love | **Ω, ω** | o as in torn |
| **Μ, μ** | m as in mother | | |
| **Ν, ν** | n as in name | | |

### DIPHTHONGS AND COMPOUND CONSONANTS

| Combination | Phonetic Equivalent & Rules of Pronunciation |
| :--- | :--- |
| **αι** | e as in bet |
| **αυ** | av as in *savant* when before vowels or the consonants γ, δ, ζ, λ, μ, ν and ρ; otherwise af as in *safari* |
| **ει** | i as the ee in see |
| **ευ** | ev as in *ever* when before vowels or the consonants γ, δ, ζ, λ, μ, ν and ρ; otherwise ef as in *effort* |
| **ηυ** | iv as the ev in *eve* when before vowels or the consonants γ, δ, ζ, λ, μ, ν and ρ; otherwise if as the eef in *beef* |
| **οι** | i as the ee in see |
| **ου** | u as in *Alleluia* |
| **υι** | i as the ee in see |
| **γγ** | ng as in *anger* |
| **γκ** | ng as in *anger* |
| **μπ** | b as in *bell* at the beginning of words; otherwise mb as in *amber* |
| **ντ** | d as in *dart* at the beginning of words; otherwise nd as in *Monday* |

Although the ᾳ, ῃ, ῳ are considered to be diphthongs, the iota subscript is soundless and the vowels are pronounced as in the table above without the subscript.

# ADDITIONAL READING INSTRUCTIONS[^16]

## (ΕΠΙΠΡΟΣΘΕΤΑΙ ΟΔΗΓΙΑΙ ΑΝΑΓΝΩΣΕΩΣ)

1. **TYPES OF PARENTHESES**: The text enclosed in regular parentheses `(...)` was written by Violakis. The text enclosed in curly brackets `{...}` has been written by the translator. The text enclosed in square brackets `[...]` has been written and inserted by the editors.

2. **BLANK SPACES IN THE GREEK TEXT**: Quite often additional information (titles of hymns and prayers as well as ritual instructions) has been added into the English text for greater clarity. The attempt to align the Greek with the amplified English text across the mutually facing pages has resulted in some blank spaces in the shorter original Greek text.

3. **SPLIT FOOTNOTES**: Because of various space limitations, some footnotes begin on the proper page of reference but are continued at the bottom of the following page.

*(Printed Page xvi)*

=== LEAF p19 ===

# ΟΔΗΓΙΑΙ ΚΑΙ ΠΑΡΑΤΗΡΗΣΕΙΣ

## ΕΠΙ ΤΩΝ ΠΡΟΗΓΟΥΜΕΝΩΝ ΕΚΔΟΣΕΩΝ ΤΟΥ ΤΥΠΙΚΟΥ[^17]

Ἡ διορισθεῖσα συνοδικῶς πενταμελὴς ἐπιτροπὴ ἐκ τῶν Σεβ. Μητροπολιτῶν, Αἴνου, Σάμου, Καισαρείας, Μυτιλήνης, καὶ τοῦ Πρωτοψάλτου τῆς Μεγάλης Ἐκκλησίας κ. Γεωργίου Βιολάκη, ἥτις ἀνεθεώρησε τὰ προγενέστερα Τυπικὰ τῆς Ἐκκλησίας, τὰ μέχρι σήμερον ἐν χρήσει τοιαῦτα ὑπὸ Κωνσταντίνου τοῦ Πρωτοψάλτου, ἐν τῇ ἐκθέσει της διώρθωσε τὰ λάθη καὶ τὰς ἀνακριβείας αὐτῶν ὡς ἕπεται:

Ἐνίοτε αἱ σημειώσεις αἵτινες εἶναι πολλαχοῦ ἐγκατεσπαρμέναι, διαφωνοῦσι πρὸς ὅσα σχετικὰ σημειοῖ εἰς τὰς μνήμας τῶν Ἁγίων, καὶ πᾶσα ἀσυμφωνία πρέπει νὰ ἐκλείψῃ, ἀρθῇ πᾶσα ἀπορία καὶ διορθωθῇ πᾶσα, ἔστω καὶ ἐπουσιώδης, ἀντίφασις ἢ παραλλαγή.

Ἡ δὲ ὥρα Θ΄ ἑκάστης ἡμέρας, συνεχομένη τῇ Α΄, Γ΄ καὶ Ϛ΄ καὶ ἀνήκουσα τῇ ἡμέρᾳ, ἥτις λήγει ἐκκλησιαστικῶς πρὸ τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ, ἔδει ἵνα συμβαδίσῃ τοιαύτῃ τάξει· διὸ καὶ ὥρισεν ἡ Ἐπιτροπὴ ἀναλόγως τῇ Θ΄ τὴν πρὸ τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ τῆς Κυριακῆς τοῦ Θωμᾶ ὡς καὶ τὴν πρὸ τῶν Ἑσπερινῶν τῆς Τετάρτης καὶ Πέμπτης πρὸ τῆς Ἀναλήψεως.

Ἐπίσης καθότι ὁ Ἑσπερινὸς ἀνήκει τῇ ἐπιούσῃ ἡμέρᾳ, μεθ' ἧς καὶ συνέχεται ἀναποσπάστως καθ' ὅλα τὰ μέρη, καὶ ἐν ἑκάστῃ δεσποτικῇ ἑορτῇ ἡ ἀπόλυσις τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ ἐστιν ἡ αὐτὴ τῇ τῆς Λειτουργίας, ὁ πρωτοψάλτης Κωνσταντῖνος σημειοῖ ἐν τῷ Ἑσπερινῷ τῆς Κυριακῆς τῶν Ἁγίων Πάντων ὅτι ἡ χρῆσις τοῦ «Ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν», κατὰ τὴν ἀπόλυσιν τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ τῆς Κυριακῆς, οὐ μόνον ἀπᾴδει, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀσυγχώρητός ἐστι, διότι τάχα ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν ἀνέστη κατὰ τὸ μεσονύκτιον. Ἡ Ἐπιτροπὴ καθώρισε καὶ τοῦτο, τῇ στάθμῃ τῆς ἀναλογίας καὶ ἀκριβείας ἀκολουθήσασα, ἥτις τηρεῖται καὶ ἐν πάσαις ταῖς δεσποτικαῖς ἑορταῖς.

Ὡσαύτως τὴν χρῆσιν τοῦ «Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε» μετὰ τὸ «Εὐλογητὸς [ὁ] Θεὸς ἡμῶν» ὁρίζει τὸ Τυπικὸν τοῦ Κωνσταντίνου διὰ τὸν Ὄρθρον τῆς Δευτέρας τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος, ἐν ᾧ, ψαλὲν ἐν τοῖς ἀποστίχοις τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ τῆς Κυριακῆς ὡς στιχηρόν, οὐδὲν κώλυμα ἔχει ἵνα λέγηται καὶ μετὰ τὸ «Εὐλογητὸς» διὰ τὸν Ὄρθρον τῆς Κυριακῆς, ἂν μὴ διὰ τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ αὐτῆς. # GUIDELINES AND OBSERVATIONS ON THE PREVIOUS EDITIONS OF THE TYPIKON

The synodically appointed five-member Committee consisting of the Reverend Metropolitans of Ainos, Samos, Caesarea, Mytiline and the Protopsaltis [highest-ranking chanter] of the Great Church George Violakis, which reviewed the previous Typika of the Church—such as that by the Protopsaltis Constantine—which are in use today, corrected in its report the errors and inaccuracies of these works as follows:

Occasionally, their various guidelines, which are scattered in many places in their work, differ on what is appropriate to be performed on the commemorations [feasts] of the saints. Every disagreement, therefore, must cease to exist, every doubt must be clearly articulated and corrected, however secondary or minor the contradiction or variation may be.

The 9th Hour of every day, continuing the 1st, 3rd, and 6th [Hours] and belonging to that day, which closes ecclesiastically before Vespers, must follow the order that the Committee has prescribed in an analogous situation with the 9th Hour being done before the Vespers of the Sunday of Thomas[^18] as well as before the Vespers of Wednesday and Thursday before the Feast of the Ascension.

Also, since the Vespers belongs to the following day, with which it is joined inseparably in all the places in it, then, on every Feast of the Lord, the Dismissal Prayer of the Vespers is the same as that of the Liturgy. Constantine the Protopsaltis, however, indicates that, in the Vespers of the Sunday of All Saints, the use of “Who did rise from the dead” in the Dismissal Prayer of the Vespers of that Sunday is not only incompatible but also unforgivable since our Lord arose around midnight. The Committee decided on this issue also, following the same standard of analogy and exactness that is observed on all the Feasts of the Lord.

Likewise, the Typikon of Constantine dictates that the “Heavenly King”[^19] should be done after “Blessed is our God...” in the Matins of the Monday of the Holy Spirit, even though it was chanted as a Stichiron in the Aposticha of the Vespers of [Pentecost] Sunday. Therefore, there should be no obstacle to its being done also after the “Blessed [is our God]” in the Matins of that Sunday, if not in its Vespers. The Committee, nevertheless,

ἧττον ὅμως ἡ Ἐπιτροπὴ ἀμφιβάλλει ἂν ῥητῶς ἀρχαῖόν τι Τυπικὸν ἀπαγορεύει τὴν χρῆσιν τῆς τοιαύτης κατανυκτικῆς εὐχῆς ἐν τῷ ἀπὸ τῆς Κυριακῆς τοῦ Θωμᾶ μέχρι τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς διαστήματι.

Τὸ νέον Τυπικὸν ἠθέλησεν ἐπίσης εἰς τοὺς Κανόνας καὶ τὰ Καθίσματα ἵνα τηρήσῃ τὴν δυνατὴν ἀκρίβειαν, ἐφ' ὅσον αἱ σημεριναὶ περιστάσεις ἐπιτρέπουσιν· ὥστε, διαγραφομένης πιστῶς τῆς τυπικῆς ἀκριβείας, ἀπόκειται τῷ κατὰ τόπον Ἀρχιερεῖ συντέμνειν ἢ παραλείπειν, ἂν ἀπαραίτητος ἀνάγκη καιρῶν, τόπων καὶ περιστάσεων ἐπιβάλλῃ τοῦτο. Ἰδίως περὶ καθισμάτων λέγομεν ὅτι ὁ ἀοίδιμος πρωτοψάλτης Κωνσταντῖνος, ὅτε συνέπιπτεν εἰς Κυριακὴν μνήμη Ἁγίου ἑορταζομένου, ὡς π.χ. τοῦ ἁγ. Ἰωάννου τοῦ Θεολόγου (κστ΄ Σεπτ.), τῶν ἁγίων Ἀποστόλων (κθ΄ Ἰουνίου), τῶν Ταξιαρχῶν (η΄ Νοεμβρ.), κτλ. σημειοῖ «τὰ Ἀναστάσιμα Καθίσματα κατὰ σειρὰν καὶ τὸ τελευταῖον τοῦ ἁγίου τῆς ἡμέρας»· καὶ οὕτως ἐν ταῖς δυσὶ πρώταις Στιχολογίαις οὐδὲν τοῦ ἁγίου ἐλέγετο παρὰ τὴν ἀρχαίαν τάξιν (καθ' ἣν ἐν ἑκάστῃ Στιχολογίᾳ παρενείρετο καὶ ἓν Κάθισμα τοῦ ἁγίου), ἀλλὰ μόνον τὰ μετὰ τὸν Πολυέλεον Καθίσματα τοῦ ἁγίου. Ἐν δὲ μνήμαις ἄλλων ἁγίων, οἷον τοῦ Προφήτου Ἠλιού, τῆς ἁγίας Μαρίνης καὶ ἑτέρων, καταλιμπάνει ὁλοσχερῶς τὰ Καθίσματα τοῦ ἑορταζομένου ἁγίου, ἂν συμπέσῃ Κυριακή. Τὸ νέον Τυπικὸν ἐν ταῖς μνήμαις τῶν ἐπισημότερον ἑορταζομένων ἐκκλησιαστικῶς ἁγίων, ἤτοι τῶν ἁγίων Ἀποστόλων, τοῦ Εὐαγγελιστοῦ Ἰωάννου, τοῦ ἁγίου Ἀνδρέου, τῶν Ταξιαρχῶν, ἔχει ἀνὰ ἓν ἐκ τοῦ Ἁγίου ἐν ἑκάστῃ τῶν δύο πρώτων Στιχολογιῶν, καὶ ἐν τῇ τρίτῃ ὅσα μετὰ τὴν τοῦ Πολυελέου Στιχολογίαν ἔχει ὁ ἅγιος.

Ἐπίσης περὶ Μακαρισμῶν σημειοῖ πολλαχοῦ τὸ ἐν χρήσει Τυπικὸν τοῦ Κωνσταντίνου τὴν περιληπτικὴν ταύτην φράσιν «λέγονται οἱ Μακαρισμοὶ» ἢ «λέγονται οἱ Ἀναστάσιμοι Μακαρισμοί», ὑποδηλοῦν οὕτως ὅτι «καταλιμπάνονται τὰ τῆς ϛ΄ ᾠδῆς τοῦ ἁγίου Τροπάρια»· ὡς π.χ. τὴν β΄ καὶ ε΄ Κυριακὴν τῆς Μ. Τεσσαρακοστῆς (ἐνῷ ἐν τῇ δ΄ λέγει «ἀμφότεροι οἱ Μακαρισμοὶ»), τὴν ἑορτὴν τοῦ προφήτου Ἠλιοὺ καὶ τὴν τοῦ ἁγίου Παντελεήμονος· ἐνιαχοῦ δὲ μετὰ τὴν Δοξολογίαν λέγει, «καὶ καθεξῆς», ἀφιὲν ἄνευ τινὸς ὁδηγίας τὸν ψάλτην διὰ τὰ περαιτέρω. Τὸ νέον Τυπικὸν οὐδὲν ἐγκαταλείπει ἀσημείωτον ἐξ ἐκείνων δι' ἃ προκύπτει ἀμφιβολία, ἔχον ὑπ' ὄψει τοὺς ἀδαεστέρους τῶν ἐφημερίων καὶ ψαλτῶν μᾶλλον ἢ τοὺς τρίβωνας καὶ εἰδημονεστέρους τῆς τυπικῆς τάξεως.

Τὸ Τυπικὸν τοῦ Κωνσταντίνου σημειοῖ ἐν τῷ Μεσονυκτικῷ τῆς Κυριακῆς τὰ τρία Κατανυκτικὰ Τροπάρια **«Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, Κύριε, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς»**· τὸ νέον συνῳδὰ τῇ...

does not find anything erroneous or doubtful if any ancient Typikon expressly prohibits the use of this penitential prayer during the period from the Sunday of Thomas to [the Sunday of] Pentecost.

The writers of the new Typikon also wished to observe all possible accuracy in the Canons and in the Kathismata, as long as today's circumstances allow it, so that, even if the exactness of the order of the Typikon has been faithfully outlined, it is up to the decision of the local hierarch to abridge it or omit from it, if the indispensable need of time, place, and situation demands it. Especially concerning the Kathismata, we say that the ever-memorable Protopsaltis Constantine, whenever the commemoration of a saint fell on a Sunday—such as, for example, the Feasts of St. John the Theologian (September 26), the Holy Apostles (June 29), the Archangels (November 8), etc.—writes “the Resurrection Kathismata in order [should be done] and the last Kathisma should be that of the saint of the day.” Thus, in the first two Sections [Stichologiai] no Kathisma of the Saint was said according to the ancient order (in which in each Section [Stichologia] was inserted also one Kathisma of the Saint), but only the Kathismata of the Saint [that come] after the Polyeleos [should be done]. On the other hand, at the commemorations of other saints—such as the Prophet Elijah, St. Marina, and other saints—the Kathismata of the celebrating saint are entirely omitted if the feast of this celebrating saint happens to fall on a Sunday. At the commemorations of the ecclesiastically more eminent celebrating saints—such as the Holy Apostles, St. John the Evangelist, St. Andrew, the Archangels—the new Typikon has one Kathisma of the Saint in each of the first two Sections [Stichologiai], and, in the third Section [Stichologia], as many Kathismata as the saint has in the Section after the Polyeleos.[^20]

Also, concerning the Beatitudes [Makarismoi], the Typikon of Constantine, still in present use, writes in many places the succinct phrase “the Beatitudes are said” or “the Resurrection Beatitudes are said,” thus alluding to Constantine's statement that the “hymns [Troparia] of the 6th Ode [of the Canon] of the Saint are omitted,” as, for example, on the 2nd and 5th Sunday of Great Lent (while on the 4th [Sunday of Lent] he writes “both the Beatitudes”), as well as on the Feasts of Prophet Elijah and St. Panteleimon. In various places after the Doxology, Constantine says “and so forth,” leaving the chanter without any direction for the rest of the service. The new Typikon does not leave unclarified any of the above issues where some doubt might result, bearing in mind the more uninformed among parish priests and chanters rather than those well-informed and[^21]

expert in the order of the Typikon. The Typikon of Constantine indicates for the Midnight Service [Mesonyktikon] of Sunday the three Penitential Hymns beginning with **"Lord, have mercy on us, Lord, have mercy on us"** (*Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, Κύριε, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς*). The new Typikon, in accordance with the formulation of the Horologion, prescribes the Ypakoe of the Tone [Tone 1–8]; only for the Sundays of the period of the Triodion has the new Typikon allowed the three Penitential Hymns mentioned above [to be done] instead of the Ypakoe.[^22]

The new Typikon, taking into consideration the many difficulties [ambiguities] herein, included the Antiphons of all the Feasts of the Lord and the [Feasts of the] Theotokos, as well as their Megalynaria, so that these may be readily available to the choirs so that no discord [*chasmodia*] may result in the Church.[^23]

The Committee, before it completes the present report, requests His All-Holiness [the Patriarch] and the Holy Synod to decide on the following questions:

1. If December 24th falls on a Sunday, whether the Resurrection Hymns are omitted or not in the Vespers and in Matins as is indicated in the Typikon of Constantine, as well as another Typikon issued in 1685 with the title “Typikon of the Ecclesiastical Service.”[^24]

2. If whenever the Feast of Christmas occurs on a Sunday or Monday, whether on the Friday before, when the Great Hours are chanted, we say the Troparion of the Forefeast **"Make ready, Bethlehem"** (*Ἑτοιμάζου Βηθλεέμ*), or that of the Eve of the Feast [Paramoni] **"When recorded in the census"** (*Ἀπεγράφετό ποτε*). This situation is analogous to that involving the Troparion of the Great Hours of the Feast of Epiphany, that is, the Forefeast Troparion **"Make ready, Zabulon"** (*Ἑτοιμάζου Ζαβουλών*), versus that of the Eve [Paramoni] **"The Jordan River turned back"** (*Ἀπεστρέφετό ποτε*).[^25]

3. Whether the Entrance Hymn of Easter **"In congregations bless God, the Lord from the springs of Israel"** (*Ἐν ἐκκλησίαις εὐλογεῖτε τὸν Θεόν*) is chanted also on the days after the Sunday of Thomas, whenever a Liturgy is performed, or instead **"Come, let us worship and bow down before Christ"** (*Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν*) as the order of the Pentikostarion indicates (see the Sunday of Thomas) and for the other Sundays of the period of the Pentikostarion as well.[^26]

4. Whether the **"Alleluia"** (*Ἀλληλούϊα*) after the reading of the selection from the Book of Acts during Bright Week is to be omitted, as is done currently by some, even though the order of the Pentikostarion states the opposite, adding even the verses of the **"Alleluia"** after the reading.[^27]

εʹ) Εἰ ὁ Ἑσπερινὸς καὶ ὁ Ὄρθρος κατὰ τὰς ἡμέρας τῆς Διακαινησίμου ἑβδομάδος ἄρχονται διὰ τοῦ **«Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ καὶ ὁμοουσίῳ καὶ ζωοποιῷ»**, ὡς διαγορεύει τὸ ἐν χρήσει Τυπικόν, ἢ διὰ τοῦ **«Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν»**, ὡς ἀναφέρει τὸ ἀρχαῖον Τυπικὸν τοῦ αχπεʹ καὶ αὐτὴ ἡ ἐν τῷ Πεντηκοσταρίῳ τάξις (ὅρα Κυριακὴν τοῦ Πάσχα ἑσπέρας).

6. The Committee also requests that the Holy Synod determine which and how many hymns from the Feast of Pentecost are to be chanted at the ordination of a deacon, a priest, or a bishop in order that the appropriate order may be established.[^29]

7. Finally, the Committee believes that upon the election of a Patriarch, instead of **"It is truly right to bless thee, O Theotokos"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν ὡς ἀληθῶς μακαρίζειν σὲ τὴν Θεοτόκον*), it is preferable to sing **"It is truly right to hymn the Supremely Divine Trinity"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν ὡς ἀληθῶς τὴν Ὑπέρθεον ὑμνεῖν Τριάδα*) and asks that this be established as a practice.[^30]

In conclusion, the members of the Committee mentioned above declare and state that the first committee did not make essential changes in the Typikon, neither did the second committee. Only fully studied changes were made upon the given formulations; all members of the Committee were engaged in presenting the material in a comprehendable manner, in the replacing of the deficiencies, in the adherence to the harmony of all the feasts so that there will not remain gaps which would cause doubts to the chanters, and, in the end, there will be greater ease in the recovering of the correct order of the Typikon for the various situations.

*(Printed Page 11)*

## ΤΗΣ ΕΝ ΤΡΟΥΛΛΩ, ΣΤ΄ ΟΙΚΟΥΜΕΝΙΚΗΣ ΣΥΝΟΔΟΥ [691 μ.Χ.]

Τοὺς ἐπὶ τῷ ψάλλειν ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις παραγινομένους, βουλόμεθα μήτε βοαῖς ἀτάκτοις κεχρῆσθαι καὶ τὴν φύσιν πρὸς κραυγὴν ἐκβιάζεσθαι, μήτε τι ἐπιλέγειν τῶν μὴ τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἁρμοδίων τε καὶ οἰκείων· ἀλλὰ μετὰ πολλῆς προσοχῆς καὶ κατανύξεως τὰς ψαλμῳδίας προσάγειν τῷ τῶν κρυπτῶν ἐφόρῳ Θεῷ· εὐλαβεῖς γὰρ ἔσεσθαι τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραὴλ τὸ ἱερὸν ἐδίδαξε λόγιον.

## ΕΡΜΗΝΕΙΑ ΖΩΝΑΡΑ

Ἡ ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις γινομένη ψαλμῳδία παράκλησίς ἐστι πρὸς Θεόν, δεομένων ἡμῶν ἵλεων ἔσεσθαι τὸ θεῖον ἡμῖν, ἐφ' οἷς αὐτῷ προσκεκρούκαμεν. Οἱ δὲ παρακαλοῦντές τε καὶ δεόμενοι, ταπεινὸν ἦθος καὶ κατανενυγμένον ἔχειν ὀφείλουσι· τὸ δὲ βοᾶν καὶ κραυγάζειν, οὐ κατεσταλμένου ἤθους, ἀλλὰ θρασέος ἐστὶ καὶ γεγαυρωμένου. Διὸ καὶ τοὺς ψάλλοντας ἐν ἐκκλησίαις, ὁ Κανὼν ἀπαιτεῖ μετὰ προσοχῆς καὶ κατανύξεως ψάλλειν, ἀλλὰ μὴ ἀτάκτως βοᾶν, καὶ τὴν φωνὴν ἐκβιάζεσθαι πρὸς κραυγήν· κραυγὴ δέ ἐστιν ἐπιτεταμένη φωνὴ καὶ βιαίως ἐκρηγνυμένη. # CANON LXXV (75)

## FROM THE SIXTH ECUMENICAL SYNOD IN TRULLO [A.D. 691]

“We will that those whose office it is to sing in the churches do not use undisciplined vociferations, nor force nature to shouting, nor adopt any of those modes which are incongruous and unsuitable for the church: but that they offer the psalmody to God, Who is the observer of secrets, with great attention and compunction. For the Sacred Oracle taught that the Sons of Israel were to be pious.”[^31]

At this point the Typikon presents exegetical comments from three great 12th-century scholars of Canon Law: John Zonaras, Theodore Valsamon, and Alexios Aristinos. Because of the repetitive, idiomatic, and often obscure language therein, only a summary of the key points of these comments is given here.

## EXEGETICAL COMMENT BY ZONARAS

Zonaras relates the chanters of his time to the sons of Israel, all being the children of God, and holds their reverence and piety in the act of worship as a model to be emulated by the chanters of Zonaras’s own time. Since the chanting in church is essentially a supplication to God, the chanters should sing in a humble and penitent manner, avoiding self-exhibition with musical extravagance such as excessive embellishments or loud voices distracting the worshiper. At the same time, Zonaras insists on good musicianship, condemning formless, arhythmical melodies. The music itself should be appropriate to the sacred place, avoiding any secular or erotic associations. He pleads for solemnity as well as artistic unity in the act of worship.[^32]

*(Printed Page 13)*

Αἱ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐκκλησίαι, οἶκοι προσευχῶν λέγονται· ὅθεν καὶ οἱ προσευχόμενοι παρακαλεῖν τὸν Θεὸν ὀφείλουσι μετὰ δακρύων καὶ ταπεινώσεως, οὐ μὴν μετὰ ἀτάκτου καὶ ἀναιδοῦς σχήματος. Διωρίσαντο γοῦν οἱ Πατέρες, μὴ γίνεσθαι τὰ ἱερὰ ψαλμῳδήματα διὰ βοῶν ἀτάκτων καὶ ἐπιτεταμένων καὶ τὴν φύσιν παραβιαζομένων· μήτε μὴν διά τινων καλλιφωνιῶν, ἀνοικείων τῇ ἐκκλησιαστικῇ καταστάσει καὶ ἀκολουθίᾳ, οἷά εἰσι τὰ θυμελικὰ μέλη καὶ αἱ περιτταὶ ποικιλίαι τῶν φωνῶν· ἀλλὰ μετὰ πολλῆς κατανύξεως καὶ θεαρέστου τρόπου προσάγειν τῷ Θεῷ τὰς εὐχάς, τῷ εἰδότι τὰ κρυπτὰ τῶν καρδιῶν ἡμῶν. Ταῦτα δὲ παρεκελεύσαντο ἀκολούθως τῷ εὐαγγελικῷ ῥητῷ, τῷ διοριζομένῳ, μὴ κατὰ ἐθνικοὺς εὔχεσθαι ἡμᾶς μετὰ βαττολογίας καὶ κραυγῆς, ὡς οἰομένης εἰσακουσθῆναι διὰ τὴν πολυλογίαν ἡμῶν, ἀλλ' ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ προσάγειν τὸν ὕμνον τῷ Θεῷ· ποιεῖν δὲ καὶ τὰς αἰτήσεις ὁμοίως, ἵνα καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ἡμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος, ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ, ἀποδώσῃ ἡμῖν ἐν τῷ φανερῷ. Ἐπεὶ δέ, φασί, καὶ ὁ Μωσαϊκὸς νόμος εἶπεν ἐν τῷ Λευϊτικῷ· Εὐλαβεῖς ποιεῖτε τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραήλ, μᾶλλον ἡμεῖς οἱ τοῦ νόμου τούτου δεξάμενοι τὸ πλήρωμα, ὀφείλομεν εὐλαβέστεροι εἶναι καὶ κατὰ τὰ νενομισμένα πολιτεύεσθαι. Ἐπεὶ δὲ παρὰ διαφόροις ἁγιωτάτοις πατριάρχαις ἐλαλήθη, μὴ μόνον ἐν ταῖς ἑορταῖς γίνεσθαι τοιαῦτα παρὰ τῶν ψαλτῶν, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν παννυχίσι καὶ μνημοσύνοις τεθνεώτων, γεγόνασι διάφορα σημειώματα συνοδικά, ἀφορισμῷ καθυποβάλλοντα τοὺς τοιαῦτα ποιοῦντας, καὶ μὴ διὰ ψαλμῳδημάτων καὶ ἀλληλουαρίων λιτῶν, ψαλλομένων κατὰ τὸ θεμέλιον τῆς ἐκκλησίας, ἐκπληροῦντας τὴν παννύχιον ψαλμῳδίαν. Ἀνάγνωθι καὶ τῆς ἐν Καρθαγένη συνόδου [418 ἢ 419 μ.Χ.] κανόνα ρηʹ καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ γραφέντα· ὡσαύτως ἀνάγνωθι καὶ τὸν εἰς τὰ Σεραφεὶμ καὶ τὸν πανηγυρικὸν λόγον τοῦ ἐν ἁγίοις Πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἰωάννου τοῦ Χρυσοστόμου, τὸν γραφέντα εἰς τὴν ἑρμηνείαν τοῦ προφητικοῦ ῥητοῦ, τοῦ λέγοντος· «εἶδον τὸν Κύριον καθήμενον ἐπὶ θρόνου ὑψηλοῦ καὶ ἐπηρμένου»· κωλύει γὰρ τὰς θυμελικὰς ψαλμῳδίας καὶ τὰς ὀρχήσεις τῶν χειρονομούντων, καὶ τὰς ἐκτεταμένας ἐκφωνήσεις.

## EXEGETICAL COMMENT BY VALSAMON

Valsamon reminds us that churches are houses of prayer. The faithful should pray to God with contrition and humility, avoiding extravagant, unbecoming deportment or attire. Similarly, those who take an active part in performing a liturgical event—clergymen and chanters—should avoid musical self-exhibition as well as theatrical effects in their ritual movement that do not fit the holy and solemn sacred occasion.

Like Zonaras, Valsamon invokes Mosaic law and the piety of the sons of Israel as an example for his time. He goes on to state that his contemporaries, having been enlightened by their faith as Christians, should be even more reverent than their Israeli counterparts. To further authenticate his plea for reverence, he refers to the 98th Canon of the Council in Carthage [A.D. 418 or 419] and to a celebratory homily by St. John Chrysostom on the proper manner of worship.[^33]

=== LEAF p32 ===

## EXEGETICAL COMMENT BY ARISTINOS

“The disordered voice of a chanter is not acceptable.” Invoking even the tradition of Israel (and by implication the manner of worship in David’s Tent), Aristinos castigates “loud, jagged voices” that distract the worshiper from meditation and from prayerful reverence toward God, for God knows the silent, secret thoughts of His creatures; He does not need this tawdry loudness.[^34]

## FROM THE HOMILIES OF CHRYSOSTOM (A.D. 347–407)

Our Holy Father John Chrysostom whose Feast Day is celebrated on 13 September, in many of his Homilies spoke concerning the order both in church and hymnology, respect and piety; from these we extract the following admonitions valuable to every Christian.[^35]

The English translation of the first selection [«Μετὰ προσηκούσης εὐλαβείας...»] from his *Homily on Isaiah 6:1* (from Migne, 1st edition, Volume 6, pp. 99–102), which was omitted in the 1990s English edition, is here critically restored:
“Let us enter herein [into the temple] with fitting reverence, lest instead of receiving remission of sins we depart for home having added to them. What then is required, and what is demanded of us? That those who send up divine hymns offer them constrained with great fear and adorned with piety. For indeed there are some who, despising God and accounting the words of the Spirit as common things, utter disordered shouts and are in no way better disposed than madmen, shaking and tossing about with their whole body and displaying manners alien to a spiritual disposition. O wretched and miserable man! When one ought in fear and trembling to send forth the angelic doxology, and make confession with dread to the Creator, seeking through this forgiveness for offenses committed, you on the contrary introduce here the antics of mimes and dancers, stretching forth your hands in an unruly manner, hopping with your feet, and contorting your entire body! What do hands contribute toward supplication when continually raised aloft in vain distraction and waved about disorderly, accompanied by violent shouting that by its forceful propulsion becomes indistinct and unintelligible? Is this what it means to serve in fear: to be undisciplined and frantic, not even understanding what you are uttering through the disorderly reverberation of your voice? But someone will object: The Prophet exhorts us to praise with a shout of joy, saying: **'Shout with joy unto the Lord...'** (*Ἀλαλάξατε γὰρ τῷ Κυρίῳ*)...”

*(Printed Page 17)*

=== LEAF p33 ===

...πᾶσα ἡ γῆ». Ἀλλ' οὐδ' ἡμεῖς τὸν τοιοῦτον διακωλύομεν ἀλαλαγμόν, ἀλλὰ τὴν ἄσημον βοήν, οὐδὲ τὴν φωνὴν τῆς αἰνέσεως, ἀλλὰ τὴν φωνὴν τῆς ἀταξίας». (Χρυσοστ. ἐν τῇ Ὁμιλίᾳ εἰς Ἡσαΐου 6, 1 ἔκδ. Migne τόμ. 6 σ. 99-102).

Ἐντεῦθεν οὐδὲν ἔχοντες ἄπιτε. Καὶ πῶς οὐκ αἰσχύνης ἄξιον; » (Τοῦ αὐτοῦ Ὁμιλ. Χ. εἰς τὰς Πράξ. τῶν Ἀποστ. ἔκδ. Migne τόμ. 60).

“‘But if you have joined in chanting two or three Psalms, and making the accustomed prayers at random and anyhow, are so dismissed, you think this enough for your salvation? Have you not heard the Prophet saying—or rather God through the Prophet: **'These people honor Me with their lips, but their heart is far from Me'**?’” [Isaiah 29:13 LXX; compare Matthew 15:8; Mark 7:6][^36]

“‘Let us then hold fast to virtue; let not these words end only in delight, and in a certain elevation of the spirits. This is not the theater for singers, tragedians, and musicians, where the fruit consists only in enjoyment, and where the enjoyment itself passes with the passing day. Nay, would that it were enjoyment alone, and not harm also with the enjoyment! But so it is: each man carries home with him much of what he has witnessed there, clinging to him like the contagion of a plague. And one indeed of the younger sort, having culled such snatches of song here and there from those satanic melodies as he could fix in his memory, continually sings them about the house; while another, an elder, being more dignified, does not do this indeed, but remembers every word spoken there. Yet departing from this place [the church], you carry away nothing! And how is this not worthy of utter shame?’” (Saint John Chrysostom, *Homily X on the Acts of the Apostles*, Migne ed., Vol. 60).[^37]

## [ΣΥΜΒΟΥΛΗ ΘΕΟΔΩΡΟΥ ΤΟΥ ΣΤΟΥΔΙΤΟΥ]
### [759-826 μ.Χ.]

Ὁ δ’ ἐν Ἁγίοις πατὴρ ἡμῶν Θεόδωρος ὁ Στουδίτης ἐν ταῖς Κατηχήσεσιν αὑτοῦ τὰς ἑξῆς διατυποῖ πρὸς τοὺς κανονάρχας παραινέσεις, αἵτινες ἀφορῶσι σήμερον τοὺς ἱεροψάλτας τῶν Ἐκκλησιῶν.

«Σὺ οὖν, τέκνον κανονάρχα, ὡς τοῦ μεγάλου καὶ πρώτου ἔργου κατάρχων τῆς θείας Λειτουργίας καὶ ὑμνῳδίας, διεγερτὴς τῶν ψαλλόντων ἕκαστα, καθὼς διατέτακταί σοι, ἀποπληρῶν τὰ καθίσματα, τὰ στιχηρά, συνείδησιν τηρῶν ἑνὶ ἑκάστῳ. Νῆφε καὶ ἀδολέσχει, καὶ δικαίῳ λόγῳ καὶ τὰς ἑορτασίμους ἡμέρας καὶ τὰς ἐπιλοίπους διέξαγε πρὸς ἕκαστον τῶν ἀδελφῶν, ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τόδε ψάλλειν, ἢ ἀναγινώσκειν τόδε, καὶ ἐν τῇδε τόδε· ἐπιτηρῶν καὶ τὸ εὔφωνον καὶ τὸ εὔλαλον καὶ ταχύλαλον τοῦ ἀναγινώσκοντος, πρὸς τὸ καὶ τοὺς παρατυγχάνοντας ἐπιξενουμένου ὠφελεῖσθαι· συναναλαμβανόμενος ἑαυτὸν πάντα εὐσχημόνως καὶ κατὰ τάξιν ποίει ἵνα χορεύσῃς ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς μετὰ τῶν Ἁγίων καὶ τῆς σῆς ἀδελφότητος, εἴπερ καταξιωθείης ἔχειν τοιαύτην κατάστασιν· εὐστόχως δὲ καὶ ἀφύρτως καὶ τὴν τῶν ψαλμῶν στιχολογίαν ἐκτέλει, ὑποστηρίζων καὶ ἐμβιβάζων, καὶ ἐπὶ λόγοις σφαλεροῖς ἐπανορθῶν, καὶ πρὸς ἓν μέλος πάντας διακρατῶν, κατὰ τὸν ἦχον τῆς ψαλμῳδίας...

*(Printed Page 20)*

=== LEAF p36 ===

...another in the fear of Christ.’ [Ephesians 5:18–21]. ‘Do you wish,’ he says, ‘to be cheerful, do you wish to spend the day well? I give you spiritual drink; for drunkenness cuts off even the clear articulation of our tongue, causing us to stammer and lisp, and distorts our eyes and our whole frame together. Learn to chant psalms, and you shall see the delightfulness of the employment! For those who chant psalms are filled with the Holy Spirit, even as those who sing satanic songs are filled with an unclean spirit. What is meant by *with your hearts to the Lord*? It means, paying heed with spiritual understanding; for those who do not attend closely merely chant outwardly, uttering the words with their mouth while their heart wanders elsewhere.’” (Saint John Chrysostom, *Homily XIX on the Epistle to the Ephesians*, Migne ed., Vol. 62).[^38]

## [ADVICE BY THEODORE THE STUDITE]
### [A.D. 759-826]

Our Holy Father Theodore the Studite addresses chanters and canonarchs, exhorting them to refine and further spiritualize their tasks. He first reminds them of the lofty, sacramental character of their ministry. He urges them to obey the established order of service and to be always conscious of the significance and the liturgical form of all types of hymns: e.g. Kathismata, Stichera.[^39]

In chanting and reciting, they should use a clear, well-rounded voice, following Saint Paul’s exhortation that everything in the act of divine worship should be done decently and in order (*kata taxin*). The chanter should exercise restraint and avoid extravagance, such as singing a very high note and then, for theatrical effect, descending suddenly to a very low note. The good chanter should help other aspiring chanters to develop their God-given talent. Thus, God will compensate the chanter’s humanly limited service with infinite blessings.

*(Printed Page 21)*

=== LEAF p37 ===

...μήτε ὑπερανάγων, μήτε καταρρίπτων, ἀλλὰ μεσότητι προσυπάγων· οὕτω γὰρ καὶ διδασκόμεθα ὑπὸ τῶν Πατέρων· θέλημα ἔχων καὶ ἔργον ποιούμενος τὰ ἀποτυπωθέντα στιχηροκαθίσματα ἐκμαθεῖν τὴν ἀδελφότητα· μάλιστα τοὺς δυναμένους καὶ προσιόντας σοι ἐν πολλῇ ταπεινοφροσύνῃ, πληθύνων τὸ τάλαντον, ὃ παρὰ Θεοῦ σοι κεχάρισται· ἵνα ἀκούσῃς τῆς εὐλογημένης ἐκείνης φωνῆς· Εὖ δοῦλε ἀγαθὲ καὶ πιστέ, ἐπὶ ὀλίγα ἧς πιστός, ἐπὶ πολλῶν σε καταστήσω».

## ΠΕΡΙ ΨΑΛΤΩΝ

Ὁ ΙΕ΄ τῆς ἐν Λαοδικείᾳ Συνόδου [364 μ.Χ.] κανὼν οὐδόλως ἐπιτρέπει νὰ ψάλλῃ ἐν τῇ Ἐκκλησίᾳ ὁ τυχών, ἀλλὰ καθῆκον τοῦτο θεωρεῖ τῶν κανονικῶν ἤτοι τῶν ἐν τῷ κλήρῳ συνηριθμημένων καὶ ἐπὶ τούτῳ προκεχειρισμένων ψαλτῶν· διότι ἀταξία ὁμολογουμένως συμβαίνει καὶ χασμῳδία ὅταν ψάλλῃ ὁ τυχὼν ἀμαθὴς καὶ ἄμουσος, τοὐναντίον δὲ εὐταξία καὶ συγκίνησις, ὅταν ψάλλωσιν οἱ μουσικῆς ἔμπειροι καὶ τῆς ἐκκλησιαστικῆς τάξεως γνῶσται.

## ΟΔΗΓΙΑΙ ΔΙΑ ΤΟΥΣ ΙΕΡΟΨΑΛΤΑΣ

Πρὸς ὁδηγίαν δὲ τῶν ψαλτῶν πολλάκις καὶ ἐν τοῖς τελευταίοις χρόνοις ἡ Ἐκκλησία διέταξε τὰ προσήκοντα, καὶ τελευταῖον ἔτι ἡ Μουσικὴ Ἐπιτροπὴ ἀπεφήνατο τάδε·

«Περὶ τῆς διορθώσεως τοῦ ἐκκλησιαστικοῦ μουσικοῦ χοροῦ διασκεφθέντες φρονοῦμεν ὅτι πρὸς τοῦτο ἀπαιτοῦνται·
1. ἐκλογὴ ἱεροψαλτῶν συμφωνούντων πρὸς ἀλλήλους κατά τε τὴν ποιότητα τῆς φωνῆς καὶ τὴν τέχνην·
2. ἐκλογὴ ἰσοκρατῶν καὶ κανοναρχῶν, τοὐλάχιστον τριῶν ἑκατέρωθεν, γυμναζομένων δὶς ἢ τρὶς καθ’ ἑβδομάδα·

*(Printed Page 22)*

=== LEAF p38 ===

## ON CHANTERS

Violakis cites the 15th Canon of the Council of Laodicea [A.D. 364], which strictly forbids anyone to chant in church services except canonical chanters who are numbered among the clergy and appointed to this ministry. To avoid disorder and musical confusion (*chasmodia*), only highly trained and experienced chanters are permitted to sing, in order to create ecclesiastical order (*eutaxia*) and evoke in the faithful holy compunction and reverence.[^40]

## GUIDING CRITERIA FOR CHANTERS

Violakis cites the following list of criteria for sacred chanting, formulated by the Patriarchal Music Committee and ratified by the Church:[^41]

1. Chanters should be selected only if they harmonize with one another in vocal timbre and in musical artistry.

2. Isokrates (drone holders) and canonarchs should be appointed, at least three for each choir, and they must rehearse twice or three times a week.

*(Printed Page 23)*

=== LEAF p39 ===

3. ὁρισμὸς τῶν ψαλτέων μαθημάτων καὶ γύμνασις ἐπ’ αὐτῶν·
4. σύστασις τοῦ σεμνοῦ καὶ ἱεροπρεποῦς εἰς πάντα τὰ μέλη τοῦ χοροῦ, ἀποφυγὴ δὲ τοῦ ἐπιτετηδευμένου καὶ ἐκλελυμένου·
5. σύστασις εἰς πάντας προφορᾶς ἀκριβοῦς, ὥστε τὸ ἀκροατήριον οὐχὶ μόνον νὰ ἀκούῃ, ἀλλὰ καὶ νὰ κατανοῇ τὰ ψαλλόμενα οὕτως ὥστε νὰ παράγωνται ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις τῶν ἐκκλησιαζομένων τὰ ἀνάλογα αἰσθήματα·
6. καθορισμὸς ἐκ τῶν προτέρων τῆς οἰκείας ἑκάστῳ ἐκκλησιαστικῷ ᾄσματι χρονικῆς ἀγωγῆς καὶ τοῦ ῥυθμοῦ, καὶ ἀναγραφὴ αὐτοῦ κατὰ τομὴν ἐν τῇ διαρκείᾳ τῶν μελῶν· καὶ
7. προσθήκη ἰδιαιτέρας γραμμῆς ἀναγραφούσης ἐν τῇ διαρκείᾳ τοῦ ψαλλομένου ᾄσματος τὸ μέρος τῶν ἰσοκρατῶν.»

*(Printed Page 24)*

=== LEAF p40 ===

3. Prescribed musical pieces must be assigned for practice, and the choirs must rehearse them thoroughly.

4. Sacred gravity and reverence must be observed by all members of the choir, avoiding any theatrical affectation or laxity.

5. Precise diction must be maintained by all singers, so that the congregation may not only hear but also comprehend the words chanted, awakening in the hearts of the worshipers appropriate feelings of devotion.

6. The proper tempo and rhythm appropriate to each church chant must be determined in advance and marked by melodic divisions (*tomai*) throughout the composition.

7. A distinct stave or musical line indicating the part for the *isokrates* (drone singers) must be added throughout the duration of the chanted hymn.

*(Printed Page 25)*

# ΠΡΟΘΕΩΡΙΑ ΤΟΥ ΤΥΠΙΚΟΥ
### ΗΤΟΙ
### ΤΥΠΙΚΗ ΔΙΑΤΑΞΙΣ ΤΗΣ ΑΚΟΛΟΥΘΙΑΣ
#### ΤΟΥ ΕΣΠΕΡΙΝΟΥ, ΤΟΥ ΟΡΘΡΟΥ ΚΑΙ ΤΗΣ ΛΕΙΤΟΥΡΓΙΑΣ
#### ΚΑΤΑ ΤΕ ΤΑΣ ΚΥΡΙΑΚΑΣ ΚΑΙ ΤΑΣ ΛΟΙΠΑΣ ΕΟΡΤΑΣ ΤΟΥ ΟΛΟΥ ΕΝΙΑΥΤΟΥ
#### ΜΕΤΑ ΠΑΣΩΝ ΤΩΝ ΠΕΡΙΠΤΩΣΕΩΝ ΑΥΤΩΝ

---

## Η Θ΄ ΩΡΑ

Ἡ πρὸ τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ καθ᾿ ἑκάστην ἡμέραν ἀναγινωσκομένη θ΄ ὥρα ἐστὶ σφραγὶς τῆς Ἀκολουθίας τῆς ἤδη ληγούσης ἐκκλησιαστικῶς ἡμέρας. Καὶ ἂν ἡ ἡμέρα ᾖ Δεσποτικὴ ἢ Θεομητορικὴ ἑορτὴ ἢ μεθέορτος ἢ μνήμη ἑορταζομένου Ἁγίου, Ἀπολυτίκιον καὶ Κοντάκιον λέγονται ἐν ταύτῃ τὰ τῆς ἑορτῆς ἢ τοῦ Ἁγίου· εἰ δὲ μή, τὸ τοῦ τυχόντος Ἁγίου τῆς ἡμέρας Ἀπολυτίκιον, καὶ ἀντὶ Κοντακίου λέγεται τὸ **«Βλέπων ὁ Λῃστὴς τὸν ἀρχηγὸν τῆς ζωῆς»**. *Δόξα*, **«Ἐν μέσῳ δύο λῃστῶν»**. *Καὶ νῦν*, **«Τὸν Ἀμνὸν καὶ Ποιμένα»**. Τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας Ἀπολυτίκιον **«Ἀπόστολοι μάρτυρες»** καὶ Κοντάκιον **«Ὡς ἀπαρχὰς τῆς φύσεως»**· τῇ δὲ Κυριακῇ ἑσπέρας τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον, καὶ ἀντὶ Κοντακίου ἡ Ὑπακοὴ τοῦ Ἤχου. Ἐν ὅλῃ δὲ τῇ Διακαινησίμῳ ἑβδομάδι καὶ τῷ Σαββάτῳ τῆς Διακαινησίμου ἑσπέρας πρὸ τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ τοῦ Θωμᾶ, ὡς καὶ τῇ Τετάρτῃ τῆς Ἀποδόσεως τῆς ἑορτῆς τοῦ Πάσχα ἑσπέρας πρὸ τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ τῆς Ἀναλήψεως, ἀναγινώσκεται ἡ τοῦ Πάσχα θ΄ ἤτοι τὸ **«Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ»**, **«Προλαβοῦσαι τὸν ὄρθρον»** κτλ. ὡς ἐν τῷ Ὡρολογίῳ διατυποῦται. Τῇ δὲ Τρίτῃ τοῦ Τυφλοῦ ἑσπέρας, πρὸ τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ τῆς Ἀποδόσεως τοῦ Πάσχα, ἀναγινώσκεται ἡ θ΄ τρίψαλμος καὶ λέγεται Ἀπολυτίκιον...

*(Printed Page 36)*

=== LEAF p52 ===

# PRETHEORY OF THE TYPIKON
### That Is:
### The Typikon Order of the Services of Vespers, Matins, and the Divine Liturgy
#### For Sundays and the Remaining Feasts of the Entire Year, with All of Their Cases

---

## THE NINTH HOUR[^54]

The Ninth Hour, read daily before Vespers, is the seal of the services of the ecclesiastically closing day. If the day is a Feast of the Lord or of the Mother of God, a post-festal day, or the commemoration of a celebrated Saint, the Dismissal Troparion and Kontakion of the feast or of the Saint are said at this Hour. If not, the Troparion of the ordinary Saint of the day is said; and instead of a Kontakion, there is said: **"The thief, beholding the Author of life"** (*Βλέπων ὁ Λῃστὴς τὸν ἀρχηγὸν τῆς ζωῆς*); *Glory...*, **"In the midst of two thieves"** (*Ἐν μέσῳ δύο λῃστῶν*); *Now and forever...*, **"The Lamb and Shepherd"** (*Τὸν Ἀμνὸν καὶ Ποιμένα*). On Saturday evening: Troparion **"Apostles, martyrs"** (*Ἀπόστολοι μάρτυρες*), and Kontakion **"As the first-fruits of nature"** (*Ὡς ἀπαρχὰς τῆς φύσεως*). On Sunday evening: the Resurrection Troparion, and instead of a Kontakion, the Ypakoe of the Tone [Tone 1–8]. Throughout Bright Week and on the Saturday of Bright Week at evening before the Vespers of St. Thomas, as well as on Wednesday of the Apodosis of the Feast of Pascha at evening before the Vespers of the Ascension, the Paschal Ninth Hour is read, that is: **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ"** (*Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι*), **"They who were with Mary came before the dawn"** (*Προλαβοῦσαι τὸν ὄρθρον*), etc., as set forth in the *Horologion* (*Ὡρολόγιον*). On the Tuesday evening of the Blind Man, before the Vespers of the Apodosis of Pascha, the ordinary three-psalm Ninth Hour is read, and there are said: the Troparion **"The Word, co-eternal with the Father and the Spirit"** (*Τὸν συνάναρχον Λόγον*, Tone 5) and the Kontakion...

*(Printed Page 37)*

=== LEAF p53 ===

...**«Τὸν συνάναρχον λόγον»** καὶ Κοντάκιον **«Τῆς ψυχῆς τὰ ὄμματα»**. Ἐν τῇ Μ. δὲ Τεσσαρακοστῇ ἀναγινώσκεται ὡς ἐστὶ διατεταγμένη ἐν τῷ Ὡρολογίῳ μετὰ τῶν Μακαρισμῶν καὶ τῶν ἀκολούθων αὐτοῖς. Ἀπόλυσις ἐν τῇ θ΄ λέγεται πάντοτε ἡ μικρὰ (ὅρα αὐτὴν κατωτέρω ἐν §16) μετὰ τοῦ χαρακτηριστικοῦ τῆς ἑορτῆς, ἧς ἐλέχθησαν τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον καὶ τὸ Κοντάκιον.

---

## Ο ΕΣΠΕΡΙΝΟΣ

### ΠΕΡΙ ΤΟΥ ΕΥΛΟΓΗΤΟΣ Ο ΘΕΟΣ

**2.** Ἀρχὴ τῆς Ἀκολουθίας τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ καὶ τῆς τοῦ Ὄρθρου καὶ πάσης ἄλλης ἱερᾶς τελετῆς ἐστιν ἡ ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἱερέως ἐκφωνουμένη εὐχή, **«Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν»**¹, ἐξαιρέσει τῆς Θείας Λειτουργίας, τῆς τελετῆς τοῦ Ἁγίου Βαπτίσματος καὶ τοῦ Μυστηρίου τοῦ Γάμου, πρὸ τῶν ὁποίων ἐκφωνεῖται τὸ **«Εὐλογημένη ἡ Βασιλεία τοῦ Πατρός»**. Ἐν τοῖς Ἑσπερινοῖς δὲ² καὶ τοῖς Ὄρθροις τῆς Διακαινησίμου ἑβδομάδος καὶ τῆς ἡμέρας τῆς Ἀποδόσεως τοῦ Πάσχα, ὡς καὶ πρὸ τοῦ καθ᾿ ἑκάστην ἡμέραν ἀναγινωσκομένου Ἑξαψάλμου, ἐκφωνεῖται τὸ **«Δόξα τῇ Ἁγίᾳ καὶ Ὁμοουσίῳ καὶ ζωοποιῷ καὶ ἀδιαιρέτῳ Τριάδι»**.

## VESPERS

### Concerning *Blessed is our God*

**2.** The beginning of the service of Vespers, of Matins, and of every other sacred rite is the prayer intoned by the Priest: **"Blessed is our God"** (*Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*),[^55] with the exception of the Divine Liturgy, the sacrament of Holy Baptism, and the mystery of Holy Matrimony, before which is intoned: **"Blessed is the Kingdom of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit"** (*Εὐλογημένη ἡ Βασιλεία τοῦ Πατρός*). At the Vespers[^56] and Matins of Bright Week and the day of the Apodosis of Pascha, as well as before the daily reading of the Six Psalms (*Ἑξάψαλμος*), there is intoned: **"Glory to the Holy, Consubstantial, Life-Creating, and Undivided Trinity"** (*Δόξα τῇ Ἁγίᾳ καὶ Ὁμοουσίῳ καὶ ζωοποιῷ καὶ ἀδιαιρέτῳ Τριάδι*).

...doxology to God,[^58] is read at all Vespers throughout the year. It is omitted, however, from the Vespers of Easter Sunday (the Agape Vespers), throughout Bright Week, and at the Vespers of the Apodosis of Pascha. From the Vespers of the Sunday of St. Thomas until the Apodosis of Pascha, the Introductory Psalm is read, but without **"Come, let us worship and bow down before Christ"** (*Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν καὶ προσπέσωμεν Χριστῷ*), because in its stead **"Christ is risen from the dead"** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη ἐκ νεκρῶν*) is chanted once from the sanctuary and twice by the choirs. Beginning with the Vespers of the Ascension and thereafter, **"Come, let us worship"** (repeated thrice) is again joined to the Introductory Psalm according to the rule of the *Horologion*.

**Patristic Note [St. John Chrysostom on Psalmody]:**  
That which the golden-tongued John said concerning the psalms in general and those of David in particular, we deem beneficial to append here for continual reading and study by every Christian, especially the clergy, for whom the Psalter is a sacred handbook:  
«For what reason was the psalm introduced into our life, and why is this prophecy uttered especially with song?... Listen. When God saw that many men were rather indolent, that they came unwillingly to spiritual reading and did not readily endure the labor it involves, wishing to make the labor more desirable and to alleviate the sense of toil, He blended melody with prophecy, in order that, delighted by the rhythm of the chant, all might with great eagerness offer up sacred hymns to Him. For nothing so uplifts the soul, giving it wings, freeing it from the earth, delivering it from the bonds of the body, inclining it toward the love of wisdom, and causing it to look down upon all earthly concerns, as harmonized song and divine melody composed in meter. To such an extent, indeed, is our nature drawn to songs and chants that even nursing infants, when weeping and distressed, are lulled to sleep thereby.... This also do women, travelers, laborers, and sailors, hastening to comfort the toil of their labors with song, knowing that if the soul hears a melodious chant, it is able more easily to bear all grievous and burdensome things.... From spiritual psalms, great is the profit, abundant the benefit, profound the sanctification, and a foundation for all true philosophy is established, both as the words purify the soul and as the Holy Spirit swiftly descends upon the soul that chants such hymns. For those who chant with understanding invoke the grace of the Spirit.... Where licentious songs are sung, demons congregate; but where spiritual songs resound, the grace of the Spirit alights, sanctifying both mouth and soul.... And just as many wealthy persons, filling a sponge with balsam, wipe their tables clean, so that if any stain remain from the food, it may be wiped away and leave the table clean; so let us also do, filling our mouth with spiritual melody instead of balsam, so that if any stain has arisen in the soul from gluttony, we may wipe it away through that melody, and standing together let us say: **"Thou, O Lord, hast made me glad through Thy deeds..."** [Psalm 91:5 LXX]. Thus those who summon David with his harp summon Christ through him within themselves. And where Christ is present, no demon dares to enter, nor even to look in passing; but peace, love, and all good things flow forth as from fountains.... Where there is a psalm, and prayer, and the choir of prophets, and a mind pleasing to God among the singers, one would not err in calling such a gathering a Church. Even if you do not understand the inner power of the words, nevertheless teach your mouth to speak the words; for the tongue is sanctified by the holy words when they are uttered with a willing mind. If we establish ourselves in this habit, neither deliberately nor through carelessness will we ever neglect this beautiful ministry, custom compelling us even against our will to perform this noble worship daily.» (St. John Chrysostom, *Homily on Psalm 41*, Migne, *PG*, vol. 55).

*(Printed Page 41)*

=== LEAF p57 ===

### ΠΕΡΙ ΤΟΥ Α΄ ΚΑΘΙΣΜΑΤΟΣ ΤΟΥ ΨΑΛΤΗΡΙΟΥ

**4.** Κατὰ πᾶν Σάββατον ἐν τῷ Ἑσπερινῷ στιχολογεῖται τὸ Α΄ Κάθισμα τοῦ Ψαλτηρίου, καὶ Θεομητορικῆς ἑορτῆς τυχούσης, ἢ μνήμης ἑορταζομένου Ἁγίου. Οὐ στιχολογεῖται δὲ ἐν ταῖς ἐφεξῆς Δεσποτικαῖς ἑορταῖς καὶ ἂν ἔτι συμπέσωσιν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ Κυριακῇ, ἤτοι τῇ ἑορτῇ τῆς Χριστοῦ Γεννήσεως, τῇ τῶν Θεοφανίων καὶ τῆς Μεταμορφώσεως, ἐν αἷς οὐδὲ Ἀναστάσιμα ψάλλονται· ἐπίσης οὐ στιχολογεῖται καὶ ἐν τῇ Κυριακῇ τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς, ὡς οὐδὲ ἐν ταῖς μεθεόρτοις Ἑσπερινοῖς τῶν Χριστουγέννων καὶ τῶν Θεοφανίων, ὅταν αἱ ἑορταὶ αὗται συμπέσωσιν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ Σαββάτου, προηγοῦνται ὅμως ἐν τούτοις τὰ Ἀναστάσιμα στιχηρά. Ἐν δὲ ταῖς ἐφεξῆς Δεσποτικαῖς ἑορταῖς, ἤτοι τῇ Κυριακῇ τῶν Βαΐων, τῇ Κυριακῇ τοῦ Θωμᾶ καὶ τῇ ἑορτῇ τῆς Ὑψώσεως τοῦ Σταυροῦ (ὅταν τύχῃ αὕτη ἐν Κυριακῇ), τὸ μὲν Ψαλτήριον στιχολογεῖται, ἀλλὰ τὰ Ἀναστάσιμα καταλιμπάνονται.

### Concerning the First Kathisma of the Psalter

**4.** At every Saturday Vespers, the First Kathisma of the Psalter [Psalms 1–8 LXX] is chanted,[^59] even if a Feast of the Mother of God or the commemoration of a celebrated Saint occurs. It is not chanted, however, on the following Feasts of the Lord (even if they should occur on a Sunday): the Feast of the Nativity of Christ, Theophany, and the Transfiguration, at which none of the Resurrection hymns are sung; likewise, it is not chanted on Pentecost Sunday, nor at the post-festal Vespers of Christmas and Theophany when these Feasts fall on a Saturday (although at these Vespers the Resurrection Stichera take precedence). On the following Feasts of the Lord—namely, Palm Sunday, the Sunday of St. Thomas, and the Feast of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross (when it falls on a Sunday)—the Psalter is chanted, but the Resurrection hymns are omitted.

**Patristic Catena on the Spiritual Power of Psalmody:**[^60]  
St. Basil the Great says: «He blended the delight of melody with divine doctrines, in order that through the pleasant and smooth sound upon our hearing, we might imperceptibly receive the profit of the words, according to the practice of wise physicians, who, when giving bitter medicines to drink to those of poor appetite, often smear the cup with honey.... A psalm is the calm of souls, the arbitrator of peace, quieting the turbid and surging thoughts.... A psalm produces friendship, unites the divided, reconciles enemies; to infants it is security, to youth in their prime an adornment, to the aged a consolation, to women their most fitting ornament, a respite from daily toil, the voice of the Church.» (*Homily on Psalm 1*).  
Theodoret of Cyrus: «For divine grace, having mingled profit with the sweetness of melody, offered to mankind a teaching thrice-desirable and worthy of love.»  
Gregory of Nyssa: «Since that which is natural is agreeable to our nature, and music has been shown to be natural to us, for this reason the great David blended melody with the contemplation of virtues, as though pouring the sweetness of honey upon sublime doctrines.»  
Behold the reasons why our holy Church holds the Psalms of David as the foundation of individual and public prayers, and why in ancient times all the Psalms were chanted, as today we chant Psalms 140, 141, and certain others.

*(Printed Page 43)*

=== LEAF p59 ===

...τῆς Ὑπαπαντῆς καὶ τοῦ Εὐαγγελισμοῦ)⁴ καὶ ἐν ταῖς τῶν ἑορταζομένων Ἁγίων μνήμαις ταῖς ἐντὸς τῶν τεσσάρων ἡμερῶν τῆς ἑβδομάδος (δηλ. ἀπὸ τὴν Τρίτην μέχρι τὴν Παρασκευὴν) συμπιπτούσαις, ἐν τῷ Ἑσπερινῷ στιχολογεῖται ἡ Α΄ Στάσις τοῦ Ψαλτηρίου, ἤτοι οἱ τρεῖς πρῶτοι ψαλμοί. Οὐ στιχολογεῖται δὲ ὅταν συμπίπτωσιν ἐν Σαββάτῳ ἢ Δευτέρᾳ, καθότι ἐν τοῖς Ἑσπερινοῖς τῶν δύο τούτων ἡμερῶν Στιχολογία οὐ γίνεται.
