...the Idiomelon: **"The first-called Disciple and imitator of the Passion"** (*Ὁ πρωτόκλητος μαθητής*) (look for it in the Litiya). The Canon of the Theotokos, that of the Menaion, and that of the Apostle: **"My darkened soul"** (*Τὴν τεθολωμένην μου ψυχήν*). After the Third Ode: the Kathisma and the Theotokion; after the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion, the Ikos, and the Synaxarion from the Menaion. The Katavasiai: **"Christ is born, give ye glory"** (*Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*); then we sing the biblical canticle with **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). The two Exapostilaria and the Theotokion. At the Praises: the Prosomoia Stichira: **"Bethsaida, now leap for joy"** (*Βηθσαϊδὰ νῦν ἀγάλλου*) on 4; **"Glory"**: **"The herald of the faith"** (*Τὸν κήρυκα τῆς πίστεως*); **"Both now and ever"**: the Forefeast Theotokion: **"Receive, O Bethlehem"** (*Ὑπόδεξαι Βηθλεέμ*); the Great Doxology, and the Dismissal Troparion of the Apostle.

3.    At the Divine Liturgy: the Typika and the Beatitudes, with Troparia from the Third Ode of the first Canon and from the Sixth Ode of the second Canon. After the Little Entrance: the Dismissal Troparion of the Apostle, that of the Patron Saint of the temple, and the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin cometh to the cave"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*). Epistle [1 Cor. 4:9–16] and Gospel [John 1:35–51] of the Apostle. At the Megalynarion: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); Communion Verse: **"Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world"** (*Εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν*, Ps. 18:5 LXX), **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and Dismissal.[^183]

4. Entrance with the censer: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), the Prokeimenon, and the Old Testament Readings. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; **"Glory"**: **"The kinsman of Peter"** (*Τὸν συναίμονα Πέτρου*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Joseph, tell us"** (*Ἰωσὴφ εἰπὲ ἡμῖν*); Dismissal Troparia: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of the Apostle, the Theotokion, and Dismissal.

5.    On Sunday at Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Triadic Canon, the Litiya of the Apostle, and the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion of the Apostle, and the Hexapsalmos. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparia as at Vespers; then the Psalter and the Polyeleos. The Kathismata: one of the Resurrection and one of the Apostle with the Theotokion. At the Third Stichologia: the Kathisma of the Apostle and the Theotokion; the Sunday Evlogitaria, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. The Canons: the Resurrection Canon and the first Canon of the Apostle: **"My darkened soul"** (*Τὴν τεθολωμένην μου ψυχήν*). After the Third Ode: the Resurrection Kontakion and Ikos (recited plain), then the Kathisma of the Apostle and the Theotokion; after the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion and Ikos of the Apostle, and the Synaxarion from the Menaion. The Katavasiai: **"Christ is born, give ye glory"** (*Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*), and the entire order of the Sunday Morning Gospel. Then we sing the biblical canticle with **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). Exapostilaria: the Resurrection Exapostilarion, that of the Apostle, and the Theotokion. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Apostle; **"Glory"**: instead of the Sunday Eothinon, that of the Apostle is sung; **"Both now and ever"**: **"Most blessed art Thou, O Virgin Theotokos"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*); the Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation has come into the world"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).[^184]

## ΜΗΝ ΔΕΚΕΜΒΡΙΟΣ

### Τῇ Δ΄.    Τῆς ἁγίας Μεγαλομάρτυρος Βαρβάρας καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου Ἰωάννου τοῦ Δαμασκηνοῦ.

1.    Εἰ τύχοι ἡ μνήμη τῶν Ἁγίων ἐν πάσῃ ἄλλῃ ἡμέρᾳ πλὴν Κυριακῆς, ἡ Ἀκολουθία αὐτῶν ψάλλεται ὡς ἐστι διατεταγμένη ἐν τῷ Μηναίῳ. Εἰς τὸ *Δόξα* τῶν Ἀποστίχων τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ, *Καὶ νῦν* *Θεοτόκε σὺ εἶ ἡ ἄμπελος ἡ ἀληθινή*.
2.    Εἰ τύχοι ἐν Κυριακῇ, τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ *Κύριε ἐκέκραξα* ψάλλομεν Ἀναστάσιμα δ΄, τῆς Ἁγίας γ΄ καὶ τοῦ Ὁσίου γ΄, *Δόξα* τῆς Ἁγίας, *Καὶ νῦν* τὸ α΄ Θεοτοκίον τοῦ ἤχου· Εἴσοδος, *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρά, *Δόξα* τοῦ Ὁσίου, *Καὶ νῦν* *Ὁ ποιητὴς καὶ λυτρωτής μου*, Ἀπολυτίκια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τῆς Ἁγίας, τοῦ Ὁσίου, τὸ Θεοτοκίον καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.
3.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν, ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανὼν καὶ τὰ Τριαδικὰ *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*, εἶτα τὸ Τρισάγιον, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ τοῦ ἤχου καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ *Θεὸς Κύριος* τὰ Ἀπολυτίκια ὡς εἰς τὸν Ἑσπερινὸν, τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ ἄμωμος, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Καθίσματα κατὰ σειρὰν, Τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου, καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. After the Little Entrance: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of the Apostle, that of the Patron Saint of the temple, and the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin cometh unto the cave"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον τὸν προαιώνιον Λόγον*). ## MONTH OF DECEMBER

### The 4th Day. The Holy Great-Martyr Barbara and our Venerable Father John of Damascus.

1.    If the commemoration of the Saints occurs on any day except Sunday, their service is sung according to the order in the Menaion. At **"Glory"** of the Aposticha of Vespers; **"Both now and ever"**: **"O Theotokos, Thou art the true vine"** (*Θεοτόκε, σὺ εἶ ἡ ἄμπελος ἡ ἀληθινή*).
2.    If the feast occurs on a Sunday: at Vespers on Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm [Psalm 103 LXX] and the First Kathisma of the Psalter, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing 4 Resurrection Stichira, 3 of Saint Barbara, and 3 of the Venerable Father John; **"Glory"**: of Saint Barbara; **"Both now and ever"**: the First Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance with the censer: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Prokeimenon. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; **"Glory"**: of the Venerable Father; **"Both now and ever"**: **"My Maker and Redeemer, Christ the Lord"** (*Ὁ ποιητὴς καὶ λυτρωτής μου*). Dismissal Troparia: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of Saint Barbara, that of the Venerable Father, the Sunday Dismissal Theotokion of the Tone, and Dismissal.
3.    On Sunday at Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Triadic Canon and the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion, the Hypakoe of the Tone, and the Hexapsalmos. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparia as at Vespers; then the Psalter and the Amomos [Psalm 118 LXX]. The Resurrection Kathismata in order, the Sunday Evlogitaria, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. The Canons: the Resurrection Canon and those of the Saints. After the Third Ode: the Kathisma of Saint Barbara: **"Having loved Christ thy Bridegroom"** (*Τὸν νυμφίον σου Χριστὸν ἀγαπήσασα*); **"Glory"**: of the Venerable Father: **"The deceit of this life"** (*Τὴν τοῦ βίου ἀπάτην*); **"Both now and ever"**: Theotokion: **"The astounding miracle"** (*Τὸ ἐξαίσιον θαῦμα*); after the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion and Ikos of the...[^185]

Ἀναστάσιμα, καὶ τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῶν Ἁγίων, αἱ Καταβασίαι *Χριστὸς γεννᾶται* καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου. Εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν *Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*. Ἐξαποστειλάρια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τῆς Ἁγίας, τοῦ Ὁσίου καὶ τὸ Θεοτοκίον. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους Ἀναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ τοῦ Ὁσίου δ΄ (τὰ εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ), *Δόξα*, τὸ Ἑωθινὸν, *Καὶ νῦν* *Ὑπερευλογημένη*, Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ *Σήμερον σωτηρία*.
4.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Τυπικὰ καὶ οἱ Μακαρισμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου εἰς δ΄ καὶ δ΄ ἐκ τῆς ς΄ Ὠδῆς τοῦ Κανόνος τῆς Ἁγίας. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον τῆς Ἁγίας, τοῦ Ὁσίου, τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ καὶ Κοντάκιον *Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*, ὁ Ἀπόστολος τῆς Ἁγίας καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς Κυριακῆς, Κοινωνικὸν *Αἰνεῖτε*, *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς* καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

### Τῇ Ε΄.    Τοῦ ὁσίου Πατρὸς ἡμῶν Σάββα τοῦ Ἡγιασμένου.

1.    Εἰ τύχοι ἡ μνήμη τοῦ Ὁσίου ἐν πάσῃ ἄλλῃ ἡμέρᾳ πλὴν Κυριακῆς, ἡ Ἀκολουθία ψάλλεται ὡς ἐστι διατεταγμένη ἐν τῷ Μηναίῳ. Μετὰ τὸ *Δόξα* τῶν Ἀποστίχων τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ, *Καὶ νῦν* λέγεται *Δέσποινα πρόσδεξαι*.
2.    Εἰ τύχοι ἐν Κυριακῇ, τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ *Κύριε ἐκέκραξα* ψάλλομεν Ἀναστάσιμα ς΄ καὶ τοῦ Ὁσίου δ΄, *Δόξα* τοῦ Ὁσίου. *Καὶ νῦν* τὸ α΄ Θεοτοκίον τοῦ ἤχου, Εἴσοδος, *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, τὸ Προκείμενον καὶ τὰ Ἀναγνώσματα τοῦ Ὁσίου. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρά, *Δόξα* τοῦ Ὁσίου, *Καὶ νῦν* *Ἀνύμφευτε Παρθένε*. Ἀπολυτίκια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τοῦ Ὁσίου, τὸ Θεοτοκίον καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.
3.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν, ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανὼν, ἡ Λιτὴ τοῦ Ὁσίου, καὶ τὰ Τριαδικὰ *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*, εἶτα τὸ Τρισάγιον, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ τοῦ ἤχου καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ *Θεὸς Κύριος* τὰ Ἀπολυτίκια ὡς εἰς τὸν Ἑσπερινὸν, εἶτα τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Καθίσματα κατὰ σειρὰν, καὶ ἡ γ΄ Στιχολογία τοῦ Ἁγίου, Τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Κανόνες ὁ Ἀναστάσιμος καὶ ὁ τοῦ Ὁσίου. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς μετὰ τὸ Κοντάκιον καὶ τὸν Οἶκον τοῦ Ὁσίου, τὸ Κάθισμα καὶ τὸ Θεοτοκίον· ἀφ’ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τὰ Ἀναστάσιμα καὶ τὸ Μηνολόγιον, Καταβασίαι *Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*, καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου. Εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν *Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*, Ἐξαποστειλάρια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τοῦ Ὁσίου καὶ

*(Printed Page 238)*

Resurrection, and the Synaxarion of the Saints. The Katavasiai: **"Christ is born, give ye glory"** (*Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*), and the entire order of the Sunday Morning Gospel. Then we sing biblical canticles with **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). Exapostilaria: the Resurrection Exapostilarion, that of Saint Barbara, that of the Venerable Father, and the Theotokion. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Venerable Father (those appointed at the Aposticha of Vespers); **"Glory"**: the appointed Sunday Eothinon Doxastikon; **"Both now and ever"**: **"Most blessed art Thou, O Virgin Theotokos"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*); the Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation has come into the world"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).
4.    At the Divine Liturgy: the Typika, and 4 Beatitudes of the Tone and 4 Troparia from the Sixth Ode of the Canon of Saint Barbara. After the Little Entrance: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of Saint Barbara, that of the Venerable Father, that of the Patron Saint of the temple, and the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin cometh unto the cave"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*). The Epistle of Saint Barbara [Gal. 3:23–4:5] and the Gospel of the Sunday. At the Megalynarion: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); Communion Verse: **"Praise the Lord from the heavens"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 148:1 LXX), **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and Dismissal.

### The 5th Day. Our Venerable Father Savvas the Sanctified.

1.    If the commemoration of the Venerable Father occurs on any day except Sunday, the service is sung according to the order in the Menaion. After **"Glory"** of the Aposticha of Vespers; **"Both now and ever"**: **"Lady, accept the prayers of Thy servants"** (*Δέσποινα, πρόσδεξαι*).
2.    If the feast occurs on a Sunday: at Vespers on Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm [Psalm 103 LXX] and the First Kathisma of the Psalter, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing 6 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Venerable Father; **"Glory"**: of the Venerable Father; **"Both now and ever"**: the First Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance with the censer: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), the Prokeimenon, and the Old Testament Readings of the Venerable Father [Wisdom 3:1–9; Wisdom 5:15–6:3; Wisdom 4:7–15]. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; **"Glory"**: of the Venerable Father; **"Both now and ever"**: **"O unwedded Virgin"** (*Ἀνύμφευτε Παρθένε*). Dismissal Troparia: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of the Venerable Father, the Sunday Dismissal Theotokion of the Tone, and Dismissal.
3.    On Sunday at Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Triadic Canon, the Litiya of the Venerable Father, and the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion, the Hypakoe of the Tone, and the Hexapsalmos. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparia as at Vespers; then the Psalter and the Amomos [Psalm 118 LXX]. The Resurrection Kathismata in order, and the Third Stichologia of the Saint. The Sunday Evlogitaria, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. The Canons: the Resurrection Canon and that of the Venerable Father. After the Third Ode: following the Kontakion and Ikos of the Venerable Father, the Kathisma and the Theotokion; after the Sixth Ode: the Resurrection Kontakion and Ikos, and the Synaxarion from the Menaion. The Katavasiai: **"Christ is born, give ye glory"** (*Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*), and the entire order of the Sunday Morning Gospel. Then we sing biblical canticles with **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). Exapostilaria: the Resurrection Exapostilarion, that of the Venerable Father, and the Theotokion. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the...[^186]

### The 6th Day. Our Father among the Saints Nicholas, Archbishop of Myra in Lycia, the Wonderworker.

1.    At Vespers, following the Introductory Psalm [Psalm 103 LXX] and the First Stasis of the Psalter [Psalms 1–3 LXX, "Blessed is the man"], at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing 6 Prosomoia Stichira of the Saint: **"Having dwelt in Myra in the flesh"** (*Μύροις παροικήσας αἰσθητῶς*),[^187] **"Glory"**: **"The beauty of hierarchs"** (*Ἱεραρχῶν τὴν καλλονήν*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"O cave, make ready"** (*Σπήλαιον εὐτρεπίζου*). Entrance with the censer: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), the Prokeimenon of the day, and the Old Testament Readings of the Hierarch [Proverbs 10:7, 6; 3:13–16; 8:6 etc.; Proverbs 10:31–11:12; Wisdom 4:7–15]. At the Aposticha: the 3 Prosomoia Stichira; **"Glory"**: **"O man of God and faithful servant"** (*Ἄνθρωπε τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ πιστὲ θεράπον*); **"Both now and ever"**: Forefeast Theotokion: **"O unwedded Virgin, whence art thou come?"** (*Ἀνύμφευτε Παρθένε, πόθεν ἥκεις;*). Dismissal Troparion: **"A rule of faith and a model of meekness"** (*Κανόνα πίστεως καὶ εἰκόνα πραότητος*), the Dismissal Theotokion, and Dismissal.
2.    At Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX] and the Litiya, the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion of the Saint, and the Hexapsalmos. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparion twice and the Theotokion once; then the daily Psalter and the Polyeleos. The Kathismata in order, the Anavathmoi: the First Antiphon of Tone 4 [**"From my youth"** / *Ἐκ νεότητός μου*], and the Prokeimenon: **"Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His saints"** (*Τίμιος ἐναντίον Κυρίου ὁ θάνατος τῶν ὁσίων αὐτοῦ*, Ps. 115:6 LXX); **"Let every breath"** (*Πᾶσα πνοή*), and the Matins Gospel [John 10:9–16]; then Psalm 50 [LXX] (recited plain); **"Glory"**: **"Through the intercessions of the Hierarch"** (*Ταῖς τοῦ Ἱεράρχου πρεσβείαις*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Through the intercessions of the Theotokos"** (*Ταῖς τῆς Θεοτόκου πρεσβείαις*); the verse: **"Have mercy upon me, O God, according to Thy great mercy"** [Ps. 50:3 LXX], and the Idiomelon: **"Well...**

If the feast of Saint Nicholas occurs on a Sunday: at Vespers on Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm [Psalm 103 LXX] and the First Kathisma of the Psalter, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing 4 Resurrection Stichira and 6 of the Saint: **"Having dwelt in Myra"** (*Μύροις παροικήσας*); **"Glory"**: of the Saint; **"Both now and ever"**: the First Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance with the censer: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), the Prokeimenon, and the Old Testament Readings of the Saint. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; **"Glory"**: of the Saint; **"Both now and ever"**: Forefeast Theotokion: **"O unwedded Virgin, whence art thou come?"** (*Ἀνύμφευτε Παρθένε, πόθεν ἥκεις;*). Dismissal Troparia: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of the Saint, the Sunday Dismissal Theotokion of the Tone, and Dismissal.
5.    On Sunday at Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Triadic Canon, the Litiya of the Saint, and the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion of the Saint, and the Hexapsalmos. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparia as at Vespers; then the daily Psalter and the Polyeleos of the Saint. The Kathismata across the first two stichologiai are said thus: after the Resurrection Kathisma, we sing one of the Saint with its Theotokion; at the Third Stichologia, we sing the Kathisma of the Saint with its Theotokion. The Sunday Evlogitaria, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. The Canons: the Resurrection Canon and that of the Saint. After the Third Ode: the Resurrection Kontakion and Ikos (recited plain), then the Kathisma of the Saint and the Theotokion; after the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion and Ikos of the Saint, and the Synaxarion from the Menaion. The Katavasiai: **"Christ is born, give ye glory"** (*Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*), and the entire order of the Sunday Morning Gospel. Then we sing biblical canticles with **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). Exapostilaria: the Resurrection Exapostilarion, that of the Saint, and the Theotokion. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Saint; **"Glory"**: of the Saint: **"Let us blow the trumpet of praise"** (*Σαλπίσωμεν ἐν σάλπιγγι ᾀσμάτων*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Most blessed art Thou, O Virgin Theotokos"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*);...[^188]

*(Printed Page 243)*

Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ *Σήμερον σωτηρία*.
6.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Τυπικὰ καὶ οἱ Μακαρισμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου εἰς δ΄ καὶ δ΄ ἐκ τῆς ς΄ Ὠδῆς τοῦ Κανόνος τοῦ Ἁγίου. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον, τὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου, τὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ, καὶ Κοντάκιον *Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*, Ἀπόστολος τοῦ Ἁγίου καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς Κυριακῆς. Εἰς τὸ *Ἐξαιρέτως* *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*, Κοινωνικὸν *Αἰνεῖτε*, *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς* καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

### Τῇ Θ΄.    Ἡ σύλληψις τῆς ἁγίας Ἄννης τῆς μητρὸς τῆς Θεοτόκου, καὶ ἡ ἀνάμνησις τῶν Ἐγκαινίων [τοῦ Ναοῦ τῆς Ἀναστάσεως εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα].

1.    Εἰ τύχοι ἐν πάσῃ ἄλλῃ ἡμέρᾳ πλὴν Κυριακῆς ἡ Ἀκολουθία τῆς Ἁγίας μετὰ τῆς τῶν Ἐγκαινίων ψάλλονται ὡς εἰσι διατεταγμέναι ἐν τῷ Μηναίῳ.
2.    Εἰ τύχοι ἐν Κυριακῇ, τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας, μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ *Κύριε ἐκέκραξα* ψάλλομεν Ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ ς΄ καὶ τῆς Ἁγίας δ΄. *Δόξα* τῆς Ἁγίας *Τὸ ἀπόρρητον τοῖς Ἀγγέλοις*, *Καὶ νῦν* τὸ α΄ Θεοτοκίον τοῦ ἤχου. Εἴσοδος, *Φῶς ἱλαρὸν*, καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρά. *Δόξα* *Καὶ νῦν* τῆς Ἁγίας *Σήμερον ἐκ ῥίζης τοῦ Δαβίδ*, Ἀπολυτίκια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον καὶ τῆς Ἁγίας *Σήμερον τῆς ἀτεκνίας δεσμὰ διαλύονται* ἅπαξ καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.
3.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν, ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανὼν καὶ τὰ Τριαδικὰ *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον τῆς Ἁγίας καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ *Θεὸς Κύριος* τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον δὶς, καὶ τὸ τῆς Ἁγίας ἅπαξ· εἶτα τὸ Ψαλτήριον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ ὁ Πολυέλεος· τὰ δύο ἀναστάσιμα Καθίσματα καὶ ἓν τῆς Ἁγίας *Ὁ νέος οὐρανὸς*, αὖθις δύο Ἀναστάσιμα καὶ τῆς Ἁγίας *Ἀναβόησον Δαυίδ*· εἶτα τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοή, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Κανόνες ὁ Ἀναστάσιμος καὶ ὁ τῆς Ἁγίας *Τὴν σύλληψιν σήμερον*. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς Κάθισμα *Χορὸς προφητικός*, *Δόξα* *Καὶ νῦν* *Ἰωακεὶμ ὁ Ἱερεὺς καὶ ἡ Ἄννα*. Ἀφ’ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τὰ Ἀναστάσιμα καὶ τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῶν Ἁγίων, αἱ Καταβασίαι *Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*, καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου. Εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν *Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*, Πάντες τ' Ἐξαποστειλάρια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον καὶ τὸ τῆς Ἁγίας *Εἰσήκουσε τοὺς στεναγμοὺς* ἅπαξ. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, Ἀναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ δ΄ τῆς

*(Printed Page 244)*

the Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation has come into the world"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).
6.    At the Divine Liturgy: the Typika, and 4 Beatitudes of the Tone and 4 Troparia from the Sixth Ode of the Canon of the Saint. After the Little Entrance: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of the Saint, that of the Patron Saint of the temple, and the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin cometh unto the cave"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*). ### The 9th Day. The Conception of Saint Anna, the Mother of the Theotokos, and the Commemoration of the Dedication [of the Church of the Resurrection in Jerusalem].

1.    If the feast occurs on any day except Sunday, the service of Saint Anna together with that of the Dedication is sung according to the order in the Menaion.
2. Entrance with the censer: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Prokeimenon. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; **"Glory; Both now and ever"**: of Saint Anna: **"Today from the root of David"** (*Σήμερον ἐκ ῥίζης τοῦ Δαβίδ*). Dismissal Troparia: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of Saint Anna: **"Today the bonds of barrenness are loosed"** (*Σήμερον τῆς ἀτεκνίας δεσμὰ διαλύονται*) once, and Dismissal.
3. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion twice and that of Saint Anna once; then the daily Psalter and the Polyeleos. The 2 Resurrection Kathismata and one of Saint Anna: **"The new heaven"** (*Ὁ νέος οὐρανός*); again 2 Resurrection Kathismata and one of Saint Anna: **"Cry aloud, O David"** (*Ἀναβόησον, Δαυίδ*); then the Sunday Evlogitaria, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. The Canons: the Resurrection Canon and that of Saint Anna: **"Thy conception today"** (*Τὴν σύλληψιν σήμερον*). After the Sixth Ode: the Resurrection Kontakion and Ikos, and the Synaxarion of the Saints. The Katavasiai: **"Christ is born, give ye glory"** (*Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*), and the entire order of the Sunday Morning Gospel. Then we sing biblical canticles with **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). ## Κυριακὴ τῶν ἁγίων Προπατόρων.

*Σημείωσις.* Τῇ ἀπὸ τῆς ΙΑ΄ τοῦ ἐνεστῶτος μέχρι τῆς ΙΖ΄ τυχούσῃ Κυριακῇ ψάλλεται ἡ Ἀκολουθία τῶν ἁγίων Προπατόρων ὡς ἐφεξῆς·
1.    Τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας, μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ *Κύριε ἐκέκραξα* ψάλλομεν Ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ ς΄ καὶ τῶν Προπατόρων δ΄, *Δόξα* *Τοὺς πρὸ τοῦ νόμου Πατέρας*, *Καὶ νῦν* τὸ α΄ Θεοτοκίον τοῦ ἤχου, Εἴσοδος *Φῶς ἱλαρὸν*, καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ, *Δόξα* *Τῶν Προπατόρων τὸ σύστημα*, *Καὶ νῦν* *Ἀσπόρως ἐκ θείου Πνεύματος*, Ἀπολυτίκια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τὸ *Ἐν πίστει τοὺς Προπάτορας ἐδικαίωσας* καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.
2.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν, ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανὼν καὶ τὰ Τριαδικὰ *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον τῶν Ἁγίων καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ *Θεὸς Κύριος* τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον δὶς καὶ τὸ τῶν Ἁγίων ἅπαξ, τὸ Ψαλτήριον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Καθίσματα κατὰ σειρὰν, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Κανόνες ὁ Ἀναστάσιμος καὶ ὁ τῶν Ἁγίων *Πατράσιν αἶνον προσάξωμεν*· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς ἡ Ὑπακοὴ *Εἰς δρόσον τοῖς παισὶ*, καὶ τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον Κοντάκιον· ἀφ’ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τῶν Προπατόρων, τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῶν Ἁγίων τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς τῶν Προπατόρων, αἱ Καταβασίαι *Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*, καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου. Εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν *Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*, Ἐξαποστειλάρια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τῶν Προπατόρων καὶ τὸ Θεοτοκίον. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους Ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ δ΄ καὶ τῶν Προπατόρων δ΄ τὴν τῶν σεπτῶν. *Δόξα* *Δεῦτε ἅπαντες*, *Καὶ νῦν* *Ὑπερευλογημένη*, Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ *Σήμερον σωτηρία*.

After the Little Entrance: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of Saint Anna, that of the Patron Saint of the temple, and the Kontakion: **"Today the universe celebrates"** (*Ἑορτάζει σήμερον ἡ Οἰκουμένη*, look after the Sixth Ode). The Epistle of Saint Anna [Gal. 4:22–31] and the Gospel of the Sunday. ## Sunday of the Holy Forefathers [Ancestors of Christ]

*Note.* On the Sunday falling between the 11th and 17th of the present month, the Service of the Holy Forefathers is sung as follows:
1.    At Vespers on Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm [Psalm 103 LXX] and the First Kathisma of the Psalter, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing 6 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Forefathers; **"Glory"**: **"The Fathers before the Law"** (*Τοὺς πρὸ τοῦ νόμου Πατέρας*); **"Both now and ever"**: the First Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance with the censer: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Prokeimenon. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; **"Glory"**: **"The assembly of the Forefathers"** (*Τῶν Προπατόρων τὸ σύστημα*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Seedlessly from the Divine Spirit"** (*Ἀσπόρως ἐκ θείου Πνεύματος*). Dismissal Troparia: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, **"Through faith Thou didst justify the Forefathers"** (*Ἐν πίστει τοὺς Προπάτορας ἐδικαίωσας*), and Dismissal.
2.    On Sunday at Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Triadic Canon and the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion of the Saints, and the Hexapsalmos. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion twice and that of the Saints once; then the daily Psalter and the Amomos [Psalm 118 LXX]. The Resurrection Kathismata in order, the Sunday Evlogitaria, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. The Canons: the Resurrection Canon and that of the Saints: **"Let us offer praise to the Fathers"** (*Πατράσιν αἶνον προσάξωμεν*). After the Third Ode: the Hypakoe: **"Unto dew for the Children"** (*Εἰς δρόσον τοῖς παισὶ*), and the Resurrection Kontakion; after the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion and Ikos of the Forefathers, the Menaion Synaxarion of the Saints of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Sunday of the Forefathers. The Katavasiai: **"Christ is born, give ye glory"** (*Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*), and the entire order of the Sunday Morning Gospel. Then we sing biblical canticles with **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). Exapostilaria: the Resurrection Exapostilarion, that of the Forefathers, and the Theotokion. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Forefathers: **"The memory of the venerable"** (*Τὴν τῶν σεπτῶν*); **"Glory"**: **"Come, all ye faithful, let us feast"** (*Δεῦτε ἅπαντες πιστοὶ πανηγυρίσωμεν*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Most blessed art Thou, O Virgin Theotokos"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*); the Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation has come into the world"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).[^190]

*(Printed Page 247)*

3.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Τυπικὰ καὶ οἱ Μακαρισμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου εἰς δ΄ καὶ δ΄ ἐκ τῆς ς΄ Ὠδῆς τοῦ Κανόνος τῶν Προπατόρων δ΄. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον, τῶν Προπατόρων καὶ τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ. Κοντάκιον *Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*, ὁ Ἀπόστολος *Ὅταν ὁ Χριστὸς φανερωθῇ ἡ ζωὴ ἡμῶν* (ζήτει Κυριακ. ΚΘ΄) καὶ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον *Ἄνθρωπός τις ἐποίησε δεῖπνον μέγαν*. Εἰς τὸ *Ἐξαιρέτως* *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*, Κοινωνικὸν *Αἰνεῖτε*, *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς* καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

### Τῇ ΙΒ΄.    Τοῦ ἐν ἁγίοις Πατρὸς ἡμῶν Σπυρίδωνος τοῦ Θαυματουργοῦ.

1.    Εἰ τύχοι ἐν πάσῃ ἄλλῃ ἡμέρᾳ πλὴν Κυριακῆς, ἡ Ἀκολουθία ψάλλεται ὡς ἐστι διατεταγμένη ἐν τῷ Μηναίῳ.
2.    Εἰ τύχοι τῇ Κυριακῇ τῶν Προπατόρων, τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ *Κύριε ἐκέκραξα* ψάλλομεν Ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ δ΄, τῶν Προπατόρων γ΄ καὶ τοῦ Ἁγίου γ΄, *Δόξα* *Τοὺς πρὸ τοῦ νόμου Πατέρας*, *Καὶ νῦν* τὸ α΄ Θεοτοκίον τοῦ ἤχου. Εἴσοδος, *Φῶς ἱλαρὸν* καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον [Καὶ τὰ Ἀναγνώσματα· τὸ Τυπικὸν δὲν ἀναφέρει Ἀναγνώσματα, ἀλλὰ τὸ Μηναῖον συνιστᾷ, ὅτι, ἐὰν ἐπιθυμοῦνται τοιαῦτα, νὰ λέγωνται τὰ Ἀναγνώσματα τῆς ς΄ Δεκεμβρίου]. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρά, *Δόξα* τοῦ Ἁγίου *Ἱεραρχῶν τὸ θεῖον κειμήλιον*, *Καὶ νῦν* *Τῶν Προπατόρων τὸ σύστημα*, Ἀπολυτίκια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τοῦ Ἁγίου καὶ τῶν Προπατόρων *Ἐν πίστει τοὺς Προπάτορας* καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.
3.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν, ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανὼν καὶ τὰ Τριαδικὰ *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*, εἶτα τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον *Ἐν πίστει τοὺς Προπάτορας* καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ *Θεὸς Κύριος*, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον, τοῦ Ἁγίου καὶ τῶν Προπατόρων. Εἶτα τὸ Ψαλτήριον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος, τὰ Καθίσματα τῆς Ὀκτωήχου κατὰ σειρὰν καὶ ἡ γ΄ Στιχολογία τοῦ Ἁγίου, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. ### The 12th Day. Our Father among the Saints Spyridon the Wonderworker.

1.    If the commemoration of the Saint occurs on any day except Sunday, the service is sung according to the order in the Menaion.
2.    If the feast occurs on the Sunday of the Forefathers: at Vespers on Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm [Psalm 103 LXX] and the First Kathisma of the Psalter, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing 4 Resurrection Stichira, 3 of the Forefathers, and 3 of the Saint; **"Glory"**: **"The Fathers before the Law"** (*Τοὺς πρὸ τοῦ νόμου Πατέρας*); **"Both now and ever"**: the First Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance with the censer: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Prokeimenon. [And the Readings: the Typikon makes no mention of Readings; however, the Menaion recommends that, if such are desired, the Readings of December 6th are read]. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; **"Glory"**: of the Saint: **"The divine treasure of hierarchs"** (*Ἱεραρχῶν τὸ θεῖον κειμήλιον*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"The assembly of the Forefathers"** (*Τῶν Προπατόρων τὸ σύστημα*). Dismissal Troparia: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of the Saint, and that of the Forefathers: **"Through faith Thou didst justify the Forefathers"** (*Ἐν πίστει τοὺς Προπάτορας*), and Dismissal.
3.    On Sunday at Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Triadic Canon and the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion: **"Through faith Thou didst justify the Forefathers"** (*Ἐν πίστει τοὺς Προπάτορας*), and the Hexapsalmos. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of the Saint, and that of the Forefathers; then the daily Psalter and the Amomos [Psalm 118 LXX]. The Kathismata of the Octoechos in order and the Third Stichologia of the Saint, the Sunday Evlogitaria, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. The Canons: the Resurrection Canon, that of the Forefathers, and that of the Saint. After the Third Ode: the Hypakoe: **"Unto dew for the Children"** (*Εἰς δρόσον τοῖς παισὶ*), and the Resurrection Kontakion and Ikos (recited plain); after the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion and Ikos of the Forefathers, the Menaion Synaxarion of the day, then that of the Forefathers. The Katavasiai: **"Christ is born, give ye glory"** (*Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*), and the entire order of the Sunday Morning Gospel. ### Τῇ ΙΕ΄.    Τοῦ ἁγίου ἱερομάρτυρος Ἐλευθερίου.

1.    Εἰ τύχοι ἡ μνήμη τοῦ Ἁγίου ἐν ἄλλῃ ἡμέρᾳ πλὴν Κυριακῆς, ἡ Ἀκολουθία ψάλλεται κατὰ τὴν ἐν τῷ Μηναίῳ διάταξιν.
2.    Εἰ τύχοι δὲ τῇ Κυριακῇ τῶν Προπατόρων, τὴν διάταξιν ὅρα ἐν τῇ μνήμῃ τοῦ Ἁγίου Σπυρίδωνος § 2,3,4.

### Τῇ ΙΖ΄.    Τοῦ ἁγίου προφήτου Δανιὴλ καὶ τῶν ἁγίων τριῶν Παίδων.

1.    Εἰ τύχοι ἡ μνήμη αὐτῶν ἐν πάσῃ ἄλλῃ ἡμέρᾳ πλὴν Κυριακῆς, ἡ Ἀκολουθία αὐτῶν ψάλλεται κατὰ τὴν ἐν τῷ Μηναίῳ διάταξιν.
2.    Εἰ δὲ τύχοι τῇ Κυριακῇ τῶν Προπατόρων, ἡ τῶν Ἁγίων Ἀκολουθία καταλιμπάνεται, διότι καὶ οἱ Ἅγιοι οὗτοι κατατάττονται ἐν τῷ Χορῷ τῶν Προπατόρων, ὧν ἡ Ἀκολουθία ψάλλεται ταύτῃ τῇ Κυριακῇ.

### Τῇ Κ΄.    Ἡ μνήμη τοῦ ἁγίου ἱερομάρτυρος Ἰγνατίου καὶ Προεόρτια τῶν Γενεθλίων τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν.

1.    Εἰ τύχοι ἡ μνήμη τοῦ Ἁγίου ἐν πάσῃ ἄλλῃ ἡμέρᾳ πλὴν Κυριακῆς, ἡ προεόρτιος Ἀκολουθία μετὰ τῆς τοῦ Ἁγίου ψάλλεται κατὰ τὴν ἐν τῷ Μηναίῳ διάταξιν.

### The 15th Day. The Holy Hieromartyr Eleutherios.

1.    If the commemoration of the Saint occurs on any other day except Sunday, the service is sung according to the order in the Menaion.

### The 17th Day. The Holy Prophet Daniel and the Three Holy Children.

1.    If their commemoration occurs on any day except Sunday, their service is sung according to the order in the Menaion.
2.    If it occurs on the Sunday of the Forefathers, the service of the Saints is omitted, because these Saints are also numbered in the Choir of the Forefathers, whose service is sung on this Sunday.

## Κυριακὴ πρὸ τῆς Χριστοῦ Γεννήσεως.

*Σημείωσις.* Τῇ ἀπὸ τῆς ιη΄ μέχρι τῆς κδ΄ τοῦ αὐτοῦ μηνὸς Κυριακῇ ψάλλεται ἡ Ἀκολουθία τῶν ἁγίων Πατέρων ὡς ἀκολούθως.

### ΠΕΡΙΠΤΩΣΕΙΣ
#### Α΄.

1.    Εἰ τύχοι ἡ πρὸ τῆς Χ. Γεννήσεως Κυριακὴ τῇ ιη΄ ἢ τῇ ιθ΄ τοῦ μηνὸς, τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ *Κύριε ἐκέκραξα* ψάλλομεν ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ ς΄ καὶ τῶν Πατέρων *Τὰ τῶν Πατέρων σήμερον πιστοὶ* δ΄, *Δόξα*

19th of the month, that is Saturday, and celebrated as follows: On Friday evening, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), 3 Prosomoia of Saint Ignatius and 3 of Saint Boniface; **"Glory"**: **"God-bearing Ignatius"** (*Θεοφόρε Ἰγνάτιε*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"The King of heaven"** (*Ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῶν οὐρανῶν*). (This hymn is the First Dogmatic Theotokion of Great Vespers of Saturday, Tone Plagal 4 [Tone 8]; the question arises why this Theotokion was designated in the present instance and not the Theotokion of the current Tone of the week [Protheoria § 8]). Entrance with the censer: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Prokeimenon of the day. At the Aposticha: the Stichira of the Parakletike; **"Glory"**: **"O thine unyielding and adamantine soul"** (*Ὦ τῆς στερεᾶς καὶ ἀδαμαντίνου σου ψυχῆς*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Receiving the supplications of sinners"** (*Ἁμαρτωλῶν τὰς δεήσεις προσδεχομένη*, the Theotokion of the Aposticha of Monday Vespers, Tone 1). The Epistle [Gal. 3:8–12] and Gospel [Luke 13:19–29] of the Saturday before the Nativity of Christ; Communion Verse: **"Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen"** (*Μακάριοι οὓς ἐξελέξω*, Ps. 64:5 LXX), **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and Dismissal.

**"Daniel, a man of desires"** (*Δανιὴλ ἀνὴρ ἐπιθυμιῶν*); **"Both now and ever"**: the First Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance with the censer: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), the Prokeimenon, and the Old Testament Readings [Genesis 14:14–20; Deuteronomy 1:8–11, 15–17; Deuteronomy 10:14–21]. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; **"Glory"**: **"Rejoice, ye honored Prophets"** (*Χαίρετε, προφῆται τίμιοι*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"O new wonder"** (*Ὢ θαύματος καινοῦ*). Dismissal Troparia: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, then that of the Fathers: **"Great are the accomplishments of faith"** (*Μεγάλα τὰ τῆς πίστεως κατορθώματα*), the Theotokion: **"All beyond understanding"** (*Πάντα ὑπὲρ ἔννοιαν*), and Dismissal.
2.    On Sunday at Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Triadic Canon; **"Glory"**: **"Flashing like lightning bolts"** (*Βολίδες ἀστράπτοντες*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Receiving the supplications of sinners"** (*Ἁμαρτωλῶν τὰς δεήσεις*, the Theotokion of the Aposticha of Monday Vespers, Tone 1); the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); the Dismissal Troparion: **"Great are the accomplishments of faith"** (*Μεγάλα τὰ τῆς πίστεως κατορθώματα*), and the Hexapsalmos. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparia as at Vespers; then the daily Psalter and the Polyeleos. The Resurrection Kathismata in order, the Sunday Evlogitaria, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. The Canon from the Menaion: **"By the wave of the sea"** (*Κύματι θαλάσσης*); the verse before the first Troparion following each Heirmos is **"Glory to Thy holy Resurrection, O Lord"** (*Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ Ἀναστάσει σου, Κύριε*); for the remaining Troparia, the verse is **"Saints of God, intercede for us"** (*Ἅγιοι τοῦ Θεοῦ, πρεσβεύσατε ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν*); at the final two Troparia we chant **"Glory"** and **"Both now and ever"**. After the Third Ode: the Hypakoe: **"An Angel cooled the furnace of the Children"** (*Ἄγγελος Παίδων ἐδρόσισε κάμινον*), and the Resurrection Kontakion (recited plain); after the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion and Ikos of the Fathers, the Menaion Synaxarion of the Saints of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Fathers. The Katavasiai: **"Christ is born, give ye glory"** (*Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*), and the entire order of the Sunday Morning Gospel. Then we sing biblical canticles with **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). Exapostilaria: the Resurrection Exapostilarion, that of the Fathers, and the Sunday Dismissal Theotokion of the Octoechos. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Fathers; **"Glory"**: **"The assembly of legal teachings"** (*Τῶν νομικῶν διδαγμάτων ὁ σύλλογος*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Most blessed art Thou, O Virgin Theotokos"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*); the Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation has come into the world"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).
3.    At the Divine Liturgy: the Typika, and 4 Beatitudes of the Tone and 4 Troparia from the Sixth Ode of the Canon of the Forefathers. After the Little Entrance: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of the Fathers: **"Great are the accomplishments of faith"** (*Μεγάλα τὰ τῆς πίστεως κατορθώματα*), that of the Patron Saint of the temple, and the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin cometh unto the cave"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*). The Epistle: **"Brethren, by faith Abraham sojourned"** (*Ἀδελφοί, πίστει παρῴκησεν Ἀβραάμ*, Heb. 11:9–10, 32–40) and the Gospel: **"The book of the generation of Jesus Christ"** (*Βίβλος γενέσεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ*, Matt. 1:1–25). At the Megalynarion: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); Communion Verse: **"Praise the Lord from the heavens"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 148:1 LXX), **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and Dismissal.[^194]

# Sunday before the Nativity of Christ (The Holy Fathers) — Case 2

## Case 2 [Violakis, p. 257]

4.    If the Sunday before the Nativity of Christ occurs between the 20th and the 23rd of the month: at Vespers on Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm [Psalm 103 LXX] and the First Kathisma of the Psalter, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing 4 Resurrection Stichira, 3 Forefeast Prosomoia: **"O all-blameless Virgin of God"** (*Παρθένε πανάμωμε Θεοῦ*), and 3 of the Fathers: **"Today, ye faithful, let us celebrate the memory of the Fathers"** (*Τὰ τῶν Πατέρων σήμερον πιστοί*); **"Glory"**: **"Daniel, a man of desires"** (*Δανιὴλ ἀνὴρ ἐπιθυμιῶν*); **"Both now and ever"**: the First Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance with the censer: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), the Prokeimenon, and the Old Testament Readings of the Fathers [Gen. 14:14–20; Deut. 1:8–11, 15–17; Deut. 10:14–21]. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; **"Glory"**: **"Rejoice, ye honored Prophets"** (*Χαίρετε, προφῆται τίμιοι*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Behold, the time is at hand"** (*Ἰδοὺ καιρὸς ἤγγικε*). Dismissal Troparia: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of the Fathers: **"Great are the accomplishments of faith"** (*Μεγάλα τὰ τῆς πίστεως κατορθώματα*), the Forefeast Dismissal Troparion: **"Make ready, O Bethlehem"** (*Ἑτοιμάζου Βηθλεέμ*), and Dismissal.
5.    On Sunday at Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Triadic Canon and the Glory of the Lite: **"Flashing like lightning bolts"** (*Βολίδες ἀστράπτοντες*); **"Both now and ever"**: Forefeast: **"Hear, O heaven"** (*Ἄκουε οὐρανέ*); the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); the Trisagion, the Forefeast Dismissal Troparion: **"Make ready, O Bethlehem"** (*Ἑτοιμάζου Βηθλεέμ*), and the Hexapsalmos. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparia as at Vespers; then the daily Psalter and the Polyeleos. The Kathismata: two of the Resurrection and one Forefeast Kathisma: **"The sayings of the Prophets"** (*Τῶν προφητῶν αἱ ῥήσεις*), and again two Resurrection Kathismata and another Forefeast Kathisma: **"While shepherds were piping"** (*Αὐλῶν ποιμενικῶν*, look for both on the 24th of this month); then the Sunday Evlogitaria, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. After the Third Ode: the Hypakoe: **"An Angel cooled the furnace of the Children"** (*Ἄγγελος Παίδων ἐδρόσισε κάμινον*), and the Resurrection Kontakion (recited plain); after the Sixth Ode: the Forefeast Kontakion: **"Be glad, O Bethlehem"** (*Εὐφραίνου Βηθλεέμ*) and the Ikos: **"Of Thy conception, O Virgin"** (*Τῆς σῆς, Παρθένε, κυήσεως*), the Menaion Synaxarion of the Saints of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Sunday. The Katavasiai: **"Christ is born, give ye glory"** (*Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*), and the entire order of the Sunday Morning Gospel. Then we sing biblical canticles with **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). Exapostilaria: the Resurrection Exapostilarion, that of the Fathers, and that of the Forefeast. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Fathers; **"Glory"**: **"The assembly of legal teachings"** (*Τῶν νομικῶν διδαγμάτων ὁ σύλλογος*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Most blessed art Thou, O Virgin Theotokos"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*); the Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation has come into the world"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).
6.    At the Divine Liturgy: the Typika, and 4 Beatitudes of the Tone and 4 Troparia from the Sixth Ode of the Canon of the Fathers. After the Little Entrance,[^195]

# Sunday before the Nativity Concluded / December 25: Nativity of Christ — Case 1

## Case 3 (Concluded) [Violakis, p. 260]

Τροπάριον ἑκάστης Ὠδῆς μετὰ τὸν Εἱρμὸν λέγεται στίχος *Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ ἀναστάσει σου Κύριε*. Εἰς δὲ τὰ λοιπὰ *Ἅγιοι τοῦ Θεοῦ* καὶ ὁ προεόρτιος Κανὼν *Χριστὸν σαρκὶ νηπιάσαντα*, οὗ ὁ Στίχος *Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν Δόξα σοι*· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς Ὑπακοὴ *Ἄγγελος παίδων ἐδρόσισε κάμινον*· ἀφ’ ς΄ Κοντάκιον *Χειρόγραφον εἰκόνα* καὶ ὁ Οἶκος *Ἔκτεινόν σου τὴν χεῖρα*. Εἶτα τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῶν Ἁγίων τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὸ ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς· αἱ Καταβασίαι *Χριστὸς γεννᾶται* καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου· εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν *Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*. Ἐξαποστειλάρια, τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τῶν Πατέρων *Πατέρων θείων σήμερον* καὶ τὸ Προεόρτιον *Εὐφραίνου Βηθλεὲμ καὶ σύ*. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ δ΄ καὶ τὰ τροπάρια *Ἄρόν σου τὴν φωνὴν ἀληθῶς* εἰς δ΄. *Δόξα* *Τῶν νομικῶν διδαγμάτων ὁ σύλλογος*, *Καὶ νῦν* *Ὑπερευλογημένη*, Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ *Σήμερον σωτηρία*.

9.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Τυπικὰ καὶ οἱ Μακαρισμοί, Τροπάρια ἐκ τῆς γ΄ Ὠδῆς τοῦ Κανόνος τῶν Πατέρων, καὶ ἐκ τῆς ς΄ Ὠδῆς τοῦ Προεορτίου. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον, τῶν Πατέρων, τὸ Προεόρτιον καὶ τὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ. Κοντάκιον *Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*, Ἀπόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς Κυριακῆς πρὸ τῆς Χριστοῦ Γεννήσεως. Εἰς τὸ *Ἐξαιρέτως* *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*, Κοινωνικὸν *Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς* καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

# Sunday before the Nativity Concluded / December 25: Nativity of Christ — Case 1

## Case 3 (Concluded) [Violakis, p. 261]

Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. The Canon: **"By the wave of the sea"** (*Κύματι θαλάσσης*). The verse before the first Troparion of each Ode following the Heirmos is **"Glory to Thy holy Resurrection, O Lord"** (*Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ Ἀναστάσει σου, Κύριε*); for the remaining Troparia we chant the verse **"Saints of God, intercede for us"** (*Ἅγιοι τοῦ Θεοῦ, πρεσβεύσατε ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν*); also the Forefeast Canon: **"Christ being an infant in the flesh"** (*Χριστὸν σαρκὶ νηπιάσαντα*), whose verse is **"Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee"** (*Δόξα σοι, ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, δόξα σοι*). After the Third Ode: the Hypakoe: **"An Angel cooled the furnace of the Children"** (*Ἄγγελος Παίδων ἐδρόσισε κάμινον*); after the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion: **"Refusing to worship the graven image"** (*Χειρόγραφον εἰκόνα μὴ σεβασθέντες*) and the Ikos: **"Stretch out Thy hand"** (*Ἔκτεινόν σου τὴν χεῖρα*). Then the Menaion Synaxarion of the Saints of the day and the Hypomnema of the Sunday. The Katavasiai: **"Christ is born, give ye glory"** (*Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*), and the entire order of the Sunday Morning Gospel. Then we sing biblical canticles with **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). Exapostilaria: the Resurrection Exapostilarion, that of the Fathers: **"Today let us praise the divine Fathers"** (*Πατέρων θείων σήμερον*), and that of the Forefeast: **"Rejoice, O Bethlehem, thou also"** (*Εὐφραίνου Βηθλεὲμ καὶ σύ*). At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 Troparia of the Fathers: **"In truth lift up thy voice, O Zion"** (*Ἆρόν σου τὴν φωνὴν ἀληθῶς*); **"Glory"**: **"The assembly of legal teachings"** (*Τῶν νομικῶν διδαγμάτων ὁ σύλλογος*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Most blessed art Thou, O Virgin Theotokos"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*); the Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation has come into the world"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).
9.    In the Divine Liturgy: the Typika, and Beatitudes consisting of Troparia from the Third Ode of the Canon of the Fathers and from the Sixth Ode of the Forefeast Canon. After the Little Entrance: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of the Fathers, that of the Forefeast, and that of the Patron Saint of the temple; Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin cometh unto the cave"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*). The Epistle and Gospel of the Sunday before the Nativity of Christ [Heb. 11:9–10, 32–40; Matt. 1:1–25]. At the Megalynarion: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); Communion Verse: **"Praise the Lord from the heavens"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 148:1 LXX), **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and Dismissal.

# December 25: Nativity of Christ — Royal Hours: First Hour Concl. / Third Hour

## First Hour (Concluded) [Violakis, p. 263]

the Patriarch (or the Hierarch) descends into the nave of the temple, and the Priest having given the blessing, the Patriarch begins: **"Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee... O Heavenly King, the Comforter..."** (*Δόξα σοι, ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, δόξα σοι... Βασιλεῦ Οὐράνιε, Παράκλητε...*), etc. The Reader says the Trisagion Prayers, and after the Priest's ecphonesis: **"For Thine is the kingdom..."** (*Ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν*), **"Lord, have mercy"** (12 times); **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**, **"O come, let us worship"** (*Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν*), and immediately the appointed psalms of the First Hour [Psalms 5, 44, and 45 LXX]. At the conclusion: **"Glory to the Father..."**, the Troparion: **"Mary once, with aged Joseph, went to be enrolled"** (*Ἀπεγράφετό ποτε*); **"Both now and ever..."**, **"What shall we call thee, O thou who art full of grace?"** (*Τί σε καλέσωμεν, ὦ Κεχαριτωμένη;*). And the First Choir begins chanting the Idiomelon: **"Make ready, O Bethlehem"** (*Βηθλεὲμ ἑτοιμάζου*). Then the Second Choir chants the Verse: **"God shall come from Teman, and the Holy One from the mountain overshadowed and densely forested"** (*Ὁ Θεὸς ἀπὸ Θαιμὰν ἥξει, καὶ ὁ Ἅγιος ἐξ ὄρους κατασκίου δασέος*, Habakkuk 3:3 LXX), and the Idiomelon: **"Now the prophetic utterance"** (*Νῦν προφητικὴ πρόρρησις*); the First Choir chants **"Glory to the Father..."**; the Second Choir chants **"Both now and ever..."**; the First Choir chants the Idiomelon: **"Joseph spoke thus unto the Virgin"** (*Τάδε λέγει Ἰωσὴφ πρὸς τὴν Παρθένον*). Following this, the First Canonarch reads the Old Testament Prophecy [Micah 5:2–4] and the Epistle [Hebrews 1:1–12]; then the Deacon intones: **"Wisdom! Let us attend!"** (*Σοφία, ὀρθοί*), etc., and the Priest reads the Holy Gospel [Matthew 1:18–25] before the Holy Doors. Following the Gospel, the Reader immediately recites: **"Order my steps in Thy word"** (*Τὰ διαβήματά μου κατεύθυνον*, Ps. 118:133 LXX) and the Trisagion Prayers; the Priest intones: **"For Thine is the kingdom..."**; then the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin cometh unto the cave"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*); **"Lord, have mercy"** (40 times); **"Thou Who at all times and at every hour"** (*Ὁ ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ*); **"Lord, have mercy"** (3 times); **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**, **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν τῶν Χερουβίμ*); **"In the name of the Lord, Father, bless"** (*Ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου*). The Patriarch recites: **"May God be gracious unto us and bless us"** (*Ὁ Θεὸς οἰκτιρήσαι ἡμᾶς*), joining also the prayer: **"O Christ, the true light"** (*Χριστὲ τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινόν*). Then immediately begins the Third Hour.

*Note.* While the Idiomela of the Third Hour are being chanted, the Great Archdeacon (or the Deacon, or in their absence the Priest who read the Holy Gospel) comes forth from the North Door of the Sanctuary dressed in a black mandyas, bearing a katzion [hand-censer] and preceded by a Lambadouchos [taper-bearer], and censes the people. This is likewise repeated during the remaining two Hours—the Sixth and the Ninth—by other Deacons. (In the absence of a Hierarch, the Priest censes robed in a phelonion).

Then the First Choir chants the Verse: **"O Lord, I have heard Thy report, and was afraid"** (*Κύριε, εἰσακήκοα τὴν ἀκοήν σου καὶ ἐφοβήθην*, Habakkuk 3:2 LXX), and the Idiomelon: **"Before Thy birth, O Lord"** (*Πρὸ τῆς γεννήσεως τῆς σῆς*); the Second Choir chants **"Glory to the Father..."**; the First Choir chants **"Both now and ever..."**; and the Second Choir chants the Idiomelon: **"Tell us, Joseph"** (*Ἰωσὴφ εἰπὲ ἡμῖν*). ## Sixth Hour [Violakis, p. 264]

4.    Ὁ Ἀναγνώστης μετὰ τὸ *Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν*, ἀναγινώσκει τοὺς ψαλμοὺς τῆς ς΄ Ὥρας καὶ μετὰ τὸ *Ὅτι οὐκ ἔχομεν παρρησίαν*, ἄρχεται ὁ α΄ Χορὸς ψάλλειν τὸ Ἰδιόμελον *Δεῦτε πιστοὶ ἐπαρθῶμεν ἐνθέως*, εἶτα ὁ β΄ Χορὸς τὸν Στίχον *Κύριε εἰσακήκοα τὴν ἀκοήν σου καὶ ἐφοβήθην* καὶ τὸ Ἰδιόμελον *Ἄκουε Οὐρανὲ*, ὁ α΄ Χορὸς *Δόξα* *Καὶ νῦν*, ὁ β΄ καὶ α΄ Χορὸς τὸ Ἰδιόμελον *Δεῦτε Χριστοφόροι λαοὶ*, μετὰ τοῦτο ὁ Κανονάρχης τὴν Προφητείαν καὶ τὸν Ἀπόστολον, καὶ ὁ Ἱερεὺς τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον· μετὰ δὲ τὴν εὐχὴν τῆς ς΄ Ὥρας *Θεὲ καὶ Κύριε τῶν δυνάμεων*, ἄρχεται ἡ Θ΄ Ὥρα.

## Ninth Hour [Violakis, p. 264]

5.    Ὁ Ἀναγνώστης *Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν* γ΄ καὶ τοὺς ψαλμοὺς τῆς Θ΄ Ὥρας· μετὰ δὲ τὸ *Ὁ δι’ ἡμᾶς γεννηθείς*, ἄρχεται ὁ β΄ Χορὸς ψάλλειν τὸ Ἰδιόμελον *Ἐξεπλήττετο ὁ Ἡρώδης*, εἶτα ὁ α΄ Χορὸς τὸν Στίχον *Ὁ Θεὸς ἀπὸ Θαιμὰν ἥξει* καὶ τὸ Ἰδιόμελον *Ὅτε Ἰωσὴφ, Παρθένε*, τὸ τέλος τοῦ Ἰδιομέλου *Σὺν Πατρὶ καὶ ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι* λαμβάνει ὁ β΄ Χορὸς· ὁ δὲ α΄ ἄρχεται τοῦ *Δόξα πατρὶ*, ὁ β΄ Χορὸς λέγει τὸ *Καὶ νῦν* ὁ δὲ Κανονάρχης ἱστάμενος ἐν τῷ μέσῳ τοῦ Ναοῦ καὶ βλέπων πρὸς ἀνατολὰς ἀναγινώσκει εὐλαβῶς καὶ κατὰ τὸ ὕφος τοῦ Εὐαγγελίου τὸ Ἰδιόμελον *Σήμερον γεννᾶται ἐκ Παρθένου ὁ δρακὶ τὴν πᾶσαν ἔχων κτίσιν*, ὃ ἐπαναλαμβάνει τρὶς, εἶτα ἐξακολουθεῖ *Ῥάκει καθάπερ βροτὸς* κτλ., τὸ δὲ *Προσκυνοῦμέν σου τὴν γέννησιν Χριστὲ* ἐπαναλαμβάνει ἐπίσης τρὶς, τὸ *Δεῖξον ἡμῖν καὶ τὰ θεῖά σου θεοφάνεια* ἅπαξ, καὶ τότε ἄρχονται οἱ Χοροὶ ψάλλειν τὸ *Σήμερον γεννᾶται ἐκ Παρθένου* ἀργῶς καὶ μετὰ μέλους· μετὰ τοῦτο ὁ Κανονάρχης λέγει τὴν Προφητείαν καὶ τὸν Ἀπόστολον καὶ ὁ Ἱερεὺς τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον· μετὰ δὲ τὴν Εὐχὴν τῆς Θ΄ *Δέσποτα Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστὲ*, γίνεται Ἀπόλυσις³. καὶ ἄρχεται ὁ Μέγας Ἑσπερινὸς μετὰ τῆς Λειτουργίας τοῦ Μεγάλου Βασιλείου.

---
³ Μετὰ τὴν Εὐχὴν τῆς Θ΄ ἡ τάξις ἀπαιτεῖ τὰ Τυπικὰ, χῦμα, ἤτοι τὰ *Εὐλόγει ἡ ψυχή μου*, *αἴνει ἡ ψυχή μου* καὶ τοὺς Μακαρισμοὺς καὶ τελευταῖον τὴν Ἀπόλυσιν· ἀλλ’ ἐπειδὴ χάριν συντομίας συνειθίσθη ἤδη ἡ παράλειψις αὐτῶν, διὰ τοῦτο ἐσημειώθη ἀνωτέρω μετὰ τὴν Εὐχὴν ἡ Ἀπόλυσις.

# December 25: Nativity of Christ — Royal Hours: Third Hour Concl. / Sixth & Ninth Hours

## Third Hour (Concluded) [Violakis, p. 265]

Second Canonarch reads the Old Testament Prophecy [Baruch 3:35–4:4] and the Epistle [Galatians 3:23–29], and the Priest reads the Holy Gospel [Luke 2:1–20], etc., according to the order set forth in Paragraph 2 above. After the Prayer of the Third Hour: **"O Master, God, the Father Almighty"** (*Δέσποτα Θεέ*), the Sixth Hour begins.

## Sixth Hour [Violakis, p. 265]

4.    The Reader, after **"O come, let us worship"** (*Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν*), reads the psalms of the Sixth Hour [Psalms 71, 131, and 90 LXX]; and after **"Forasmuch as we have no boldness"** (*Ὅτι οὐκ ἔχομεν παρρησίαν*), the First Choir begins chanting the Idiomelon: **"Come, ye faithful, let us be inspired divinely"** (*Δεῦτε πιστοὶ ἐπαρθῶμεν ἐνθέως*). Then the Second Choir chants the Verse: **"O Lord, I have heard Thy report, and was afraid"** (*Κύριε, εἰσακήκοα τὴν ἀκοήν σου καὶ ἐφοβήθην*, Habakkuk 3:2 LXX), and the Idiomelon: **"Hear, O heaven, and give ear, O earth"** (*Ἄκουε, οὐρανέ*); the First Choir chants **"Glory to the Father... Both now and ever..."**; then the Second and First Choirs together chant the Idiomelon: **"Come, ye Christ-bearing peoples"** (*Δεῦτε, χριστοφόροι λαοί*). After this, the Canonarch reads the Old Testament Prophecy [Isaiah 7:10–16; 8:1–4, 9–10] and the Epistle [Hebrews 2:11–18], and the Priest reads the Holy Gospel [Matthew 2:1–12]. After the Prayer of the Sixth Hour: **"O God and Lord of powers"** (*Θεὲ καὶ Κύριε τῶν δυνάμεων*), the Ninth Hour begins.

## Ninth Hour [Violakis, p. 265]

5.    The Reader recites **"O come, let us worship"** (*Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν*) thrice and reads the psalms of the Ninth Hour [Psalms 109, 110, and 85 LXX]; and after **"He Who for our sake was born of a Virgin"** (*Ὁ δι’ ἡμᾶς γεννηθείς*), the Second Choir begins chanting the Idiomelon: **"Herod was struck with amazement"** (*Ἐξεπλήττετο ὁ Ἡρώδης*). Then the First Choir chants the Verse: **"God shall come from Teman, and the Holy One from the mountain overshadowed and densely forested"** (*Ὁ Θεὸς ἀπὸ Θαιμὰν ἥξει, καὶ ὁ Ἅγιος ἐξ ὄρους κατασκίου δασέος*, Habakkuk 3:3 LXX), and the Idiomelon: **"When Joseph, O Virgin, was wounded with sorrow"** (*Ὅτε Ἰωσήφ, Παρθένε*); the Second Choir takes up the conclusion of the Idiomelon: **"Together with the Father and the Holy Spirit"** (*Σὺν Πατρὶ καὶ Ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι*); the First Choir begins **"Glory to the Father..."**; the Second Choir says **"Both now and ever..."**. Then the Canonarch, standing in the midst of the nave and facing eastward, recites reverently in the cantillation style of the Gospel the Idiomelon: **"Today He Who holds all creation in the hollow of His hand is born of a Virgin"** (*Σήμερον γεννᾶται ἐκ Παρθένου ὁ δρακὶ τὴν πᾶσαν ἔχων κτίσιν*), repeating it thrice; he then continues: **"He Who in essence cannot be touched is wrapped in swaddling clothes as a mortal..."** (*Ῥάκει καθάπερ βροτὸς*), etc.; he likewise repeats thrice: **"We worship Thy Nativity, O Christ"** (*Προσκυνοῦμέν σου τὴν γέννησιν, Χριστέ*), and once: **"Show us also Thy divine Theophany"** (*Δεῖξον ἡμῖν καὶ τὰ θεῖά σου Θεοφάνεια*). And then the Choirs begin chanting **"Today He is born of a Virgin"** (*Σήμερον γεννᾶται ἐκ Παρθένου*) slowly and solemnly with melody. Following this, the Canonarch reads the Old Testament Prophecy [Isaiah 9:6–7] and the Epistle [Hebrews 2:1–10], and the Priest reads the Holy Gospel [Matthew 2:13–23]. After the Prayer of the Ninth Hour: **"O Master, Lord Jesus Christ our God"** (*Δέσποτα Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστέ*), the Dismissal takes place.³ And Great Vespers joined with the Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great begins.

*Note.* After the Prayer of the Ninth Hour, the liturgical order prescribes the Typika recited plain—namely, **"Bless the Lord, O my soul"** [Psalm 102 LXX], **"Praise the Lord, O my soul"** [Psalm 145 LXX], the Beatitudes, and finally the Dismissal. But because, for the sake of brevity, it has already become customary to omit them, for this reason the Dismissal is noted above immediately following the Prayer.[^199]

*(Printed Page 265)*

## Ὁ Μέγας Ἑσπερινὸς καὶ ἡ Λειτουργία τοῦ Μεγάλου Βασιλείου [Violakis, p. 266]

6.    Ὁ Διάκονος *Εὐλόγησον Δέσποτα*, ὁ Ἱερεὺς *Εὐλογημένη ἡ βασιλεία*, ὁ Πατριάρχης (ἢ ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς) τὸν Προοιμιακὸν, εἰς τὸ *Κύριε ἐκέκραξα* ψάλλομεν τὰ δ΄ Ἰδιόμελα *Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα τῷ Κυρίῳ* εἰς ς΄. *Δόξα Καὶ νῦν* *Αὐγούστου μοναρχήσαντος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς*, Εἴσοδος μετὰ Εὐαγγελίου, *Φῶς ἱλαρὸν* καὶ εὐθὺς ὁ Κανονάρχης τὸ Α΄ Ἀνάγνωσμα *Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν*, μετὰ τὸ τέλος ἄρχεται ὁ α΄ Χορὸς ψάλλειν τὸ Τροπάριον *Λαθὼν ἐτέχθης* καὶ ὁ β΄ Χορὸς ἐπαναλαμβάνει *Καὶ μάγους σοι προσήνεγκεν*· τὸ αὐτὸ ἐπαναλαμβάνουσιν ἑκατέρωθεν οἱ Χοροὶ, ἕως οὗ ὁ Κανονάρχης πληρώσῃ τοὺς Στίχους τοῦ ψαλμοῦ· εἶτα ὁ α΄ Χορὸς *Δόξα Καὶ νῦν* καὶ ψάλλει αὖθις τὸ Τροπάριον ὁλόκληρον. Ἀκολούθως ὁ β΄ Κανονάρχης ἀναγινώσκει τὸ Ζ΄ Ἀνάγνωσμα *Παιδίον ἐγεννήθη ἡμῖν*, μετὰ τὸ τέλος ὁ β΄ Χορὸς ψάλλει τὸ Τροπάριον *Ἀνέτειλας Χριστὲ ἐκ Παρθένου*, τὸ τέλος δὲ καὶ τούτου *Μάγους ὁδηγήσας* ἐπαναλαμβάνεται ὑπὸ τῶν δύο Χορῶν, ἕως οὗ ὁ Κανονάρχης πληρώσῃ τοὺς Στίχους τοῦ ψαλμοῦ ὡς ἀνωτέρω· εἶτα ὁ β΄ Χορὸς *Δόξα Καὶ νῦν* ἐπαναλαμβάνων ὁλόκληρον τὸ Τροπάριον, καὶ ὁ α΄ Κανονάρχης ἀναγινώσκει τὸ Η΄ Ἀνάγνωσμα *Προέθετο Κύριος λαλῆσαι τῷ Ἄχαζ*· μετὰ ταῦτα ἡ μικρὰ Συναπτὴ *Τοῦ Κυρίου δεηθῶμεν* κτλ. καὶ ψάλλεται ὁ Τρισάγιος ὕμνος, ὁ Ἀπόστολος, τὸ Ἀλληλούϊα καὶ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον ἀπ’ Ἄμβωνος ὑπὸ τοῦ Διακόνου· μετὰ τὸ τέλος ὁ Πατριάρχης (ἢ ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς) εὐλογεῖ τὸν λαὸν, τῶν Χορῶν ψαλλόντων *Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*· εἰδεμὴ, λέγεται τὸ, *Δόξα σοι Κύριε, Δόξα σοι* καὶ καθεξῆς ἡ Λειτουργία τοῦ Μ. Βασιλείου, Κοινωνικὸν *Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς* καὶ ἡ Ἀπόλυσις μετὰ τοῦ *Ὁ ἐν σπηλαίῳ γεννηθεὶς καὶ ἐν φάτνῃ ἀνακληθεὶς διὰ τὴν ἡμῶν σωτηρίαν Χριστὸς ὁ ἀληθινός . . . .*

# December 25: Nativity of Christ — Vespers & Liturgy of St. Basil / Matins of the Feast

## Great Vespers and the Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great [Violakis, p. 267]

6.    The Deacon: **"Master, bless"** (*Εὐλόγησον, Δέσποτα*); the Priest: **"Blessed is the kingdom of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit"** (*Εὐλογημένη ἡ βασιλεία*); the Patriarch (or the Hierarch) recites the Introductory Psalm [Psalm 103 LXX]. At **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing the 4 Idiomela: **"Come, let us rejoice in the Lord"** (*Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα τῷ Κυρίῳ*) in 6 (repeating the first two). **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**: **"When Augustus reigned alone upon the earth"** (*Αὐγούστου μοναρχήσαντος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς*). Entrance is made with the Holy Gospel; **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and immediately the Canonarch intones the First Old Testament Reading: **"In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth"** (*Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεὸς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν*, Genesis 1:1–13). At the conclusion, the First Choir begins chanting the Troparion: **"Having been born secretly in a cave"** (*Λαθὼν ἐτέχθης ὑπὸ τὸ σπήλαιον*), and the Second Choir responds with the refrain: **"And brought the Magi unto Thee"** (*Καὶ μάγους σοι προσήνεγκεν*); this same refrain the Choirs repeat alternately on each side until the Canonarch completes the verses of the Psalm; then the First Choir chants **"Glory... Both now and ever..."** and sings the entire Troparion again from the beginning. Thereupon the Second Canonarch reads the Seventh Reading: **"A Child is born unto us, a Son is given unto us"** (*Παιδίον ἐγεννήθη ἡμῖν*, Isaiah 9:6–7); at the conclusion, the Second Choir chants the Troparion: **"Thou didst dawn forth, O Christ, from a Virgin"** (*Ἀνέτειλας Χριστὲ ἐκ Παρθένου*), and the conclusion thereof: **"Having guided the Magi by a star"** (*Μάγους ὁδηγήσας*) is repeated by both Choirs until the Canonarch completes the verses of the Psalm as above; then the Second Choir chants **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**, repeating the entire Troparion; and the First Canonarch reads the Eighth Reading: **"The Lord spoke again to Ahaz"** (*Προέθετο Κύριος λαλῆσαι τῷ Ἄχαζ*, Isaiah 7:10–16; 8:1–4, 9–10). After these readings, the Little Litany: **"Let us pray to the Lord"** (*Τοῦ Κυρίου δεηθῶμεν*), etc., and the Trisagion Hymn is sung; then the Epistle [Hebrews 1:1–12], the Alleluia [Ps. 109:1 LXX], and the Holy Gospel [Luke 2:1–20] proclaimed from the Ambo by the Deacon. At the conclusion, the Patriarch (or the Hierarch) blesses the people, the Choirs chanting: **"Many years, Master"** (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη, Δέσποτα*); otherwise, there is said: **"Glory to Thee, O Lord, glory to Thee"** (*Δόξα σοι, Κύριε, δόξα σοι*), and the Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great follows in order; Communion Verse: **"Praise the Lord from the heavens"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 148:1 LXX), **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and the Dismissal with the proper festal incipit: **"May He Who was born in a cave and lay in a manger for our salvation, Christ our true God..."** (*Ὁ ἐν σπηλαίῳ γεννηθεὶς καὶ ἐν φάτνῃ ἀνακληθεὶς διὰ τὴν ἡμῶν σωτηρίαν Χριστὸς ὁ ἀληθινὸς Θεὸς ἡμῶν...*).
7.    On Friday at Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Lite and the Idiomela of the Aposticha (since they were not sung yesterday); then the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"** (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου, Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*), and the Hexapsalmos. At **"God is the...**

*Note.* The Typikon of Constantine prescribes for this day the Dismissal Troparion of the Feast: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God..."** instead of **"We have seen the true light"**; but neither the ancient Typikon nor the rubrics in the Menaion mention such a thing; therefore it has been approved that **"We have seen the true light"** be sung, which is replaced by the Dismissal Troparion only after the Liturgy of the principal day of each Master's Feast.[^200]

*(Printed Page 267)*

## Ὄρθρος τῆς Ἑορτῆς (Συνέχεια) [Violakis, p. 268]

*Κύριος* τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον *Ἡ γέννησίς σου* ἐκ τρίτου, εἶτα τὸ Ψαλτήριον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ ὁ Πολυέλεος *Αἰνεῖτε τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*, τὰ γ΄ Καθίσματα κατὰ σειρὰν, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ, τὸ α΄ Ἀντίφωνον τοῦ δ΄ Ἤχου, τὸ Προκείμενον *Ἐκ γαστρὸς πρὸ Ἑωσφόρου ἐγέννησά σε, ὤμοσε Κύριος καὶ οὐ μεταμεληθήσεται*, τὸ *Πᾶσα πνοὴ* καὶ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον, εἶτα ὁ Ν΄ ψαλμὸς χῦμα, *Δόξα* *Τὰ σύμπαντα σήμερον χαρᾶς πληροῦνται*, *Καὶ νῦν* τὸ αὐτό, Στίχος *Ἐλέησόν με ὁ Θεὸς* καὶ τὸ Ἰδιόμελον *Δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις Θεῷ* (ζήτει ἐν τῷ Ἑσπερινῷ τῆς ΚΣΤ΄). Οἱ Κανόνες ἀμφότεροι ἀνὰ δ΄ Τροπάρια ἄνευ Στίχων, εἰς τὰ δύο τελευταῖα *Δόξα Καὶ νῦν*· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ χῦμα, ἀφ’ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον, ὁ Οἶκος καὶ τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῆς ἑορτῆς· αἱ Καταβασίαι διπλαῖ μέχρις η΄ Ὠδῆς, εἶτα ψάλλεται ἡ θ΄ Ὠδὴ μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων ὡς ἑξῆς·

Διὰ τὸν α΄ Κανόνα

*Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὴν τιμιωτέραν, καὶ ἐνδοξοτέραν τῶν ἄνω στρατευμάτων.*  
*Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὸν ἐκ τῆς Παρθένου, θεὸν σαρκὶ τεχθέντα.*  
*Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὸν ἐν τῷ Σπηλαίῳ, τεχθέντα βασιλέα.*  
*Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὸν ὑπὸ τῶν Μάγων, θεὸν προσκυνηθέντα.*  

Διὰ τὸν β΄ Ἰαμβικόν

*Σήμερον ἡ Παρθένος, τίκτει τὸν Δεσπότην, ἔνδον ἐν τῷ Σπηλαίῳ.*  
*Σήμερον ὁ Δεσπότης, τίκτεται ὡς βρέφος, ὑπὸ Μητρὸς Παρθένου.*  
*Δόξα, Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τῆς Τρισυποστάτου, καὶ ἀδιαιρέτου, θεότητος τὸ κράτος.*  
*Καὶ νῦν, Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὴν λυτρωσαμένην, ἡμᾶς ἐκ τῆς κατάρας.*  

Αἱ δύο Καταβασίαι τῆς θ΄, καὶ τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον *Ἐπεσκέψατο ἡμᾶς* ἐκ γ΄. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, τὰ δ΄ Ἰδιόμελα *Εὐφραίνεσθε, δίκαιοι.*

# December 25: Nativity of Christ — Matins of the Feast Concluded

## Matins of the Feast (Concluded) [Violakis, p. 269]

Lord" (*Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"** (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου, Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*) thrice; then the daily Psalter and the Polyeleos: **"Praise ye the name of the Lord"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*, Psalms 134–135 LXX). The three Kathismata are sung in order; the Anavathmoi: the First Antiphon of Tone 4; and the Prokeimenon in Tone 4: **"From the womb before the morning star have I begotten Thee; the Lord hath sworn, and will not repent"** (*Ἐκ γαστρὸς πρὸ Ἑωσφόρου ἐγέννησά σε, ὤμοσε Κύριος καὶ οὐ μεταμεληθήσεται*, Ps. 109:3–4 LXX); then **"Let every breath praise the Lord"** (*Πᾶσα πνοή*) and the Matins Gospel [Matthew 1:18–25]; then Psalm 50 [LXX] recited plain; **"Glory"**: **"All things are filled with joy today"** (*Τὰ σύμπαντα σήμερον χαρᾶς πληροῦνται*); **"Both now and ever"**: repeat the same. The Verse: **"Have mercy on me, O God, according to Thy great mercy"** (*Ἐλέησόν με, ὁ Θεός*, Ps. 50:1 LXX) and the Idiomelon: **"Glory to God in the highest"** (*Δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις Θεῷ*, look at Vespers of December 26). Both Canons are sung with four Troparia each without verses, but at the last two Troparia we chant the verse **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**. After the Third Ode: the Hypakoe (recited plain) [**"The heavens brought an offering"** / *Τὴν ἀπαρχὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν*]; after the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin cometh to the cave"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*), the Ikos, and the Synaxarion of the Feast. The double Katavasiai are sung through the Eighth Ode; then the Ninth Ode is sung with the Megalynaria as follows:

### For the First Canon

*Magnify, O my soul, her who is greater in honor and more glorious than the hosts on high.*  
*Magnify, O my soul, God born in the flesh from the Virgin.*  
*Magnify, O my soul, the King born in the cave.*  
*Magnify, O my soul, God worshipped by the Magi.*  

### For the Second (Iambic) Canon

*Today the Virgin gives birth to the Master within the cave.*  
*Today the Master is born as a babe from a Virgin Mother.*  
*Glory to the Father... Magnify, O my soul, the power of the three-hypostatic and undivided Godhead.*  
*Both now and ever... Magnify, O my soul, her who has delivered us from the curse.*  

The two Katavasiai of the Ninth Ode, and the Exapostilarion: **"Our Savior, the Dayspring from on high, hath visited us"** (*Ἐπεσκέψατο ἡμᾶς*) thrice. At the Praises: the 4 Idiomela: **"Be glad, O ye righteous"** (*Εὐφραίνεσθε, δίκαιοι*)...[^201]

righteous" (*Εὐφραίνεσθε, δίκαιοι*); **"Glory"**: **"When it was time for Thy coming upon earth"** (*Ὅτε καιρὸς τῆς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς παρουσίας σου*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Today Christ is born in Bethlehem of the Virgin"** (*Σήμερον ὁ Χριστὸς*) up to the cue words **"and we cry aloud without ceasing"** (*ἡμεῖς δὲ ἀκαταπαύστως βοῶμεν*); and the Great Doxology begins immediately: **"Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will among men."** (Note: In other words, the final phrase of the above Theotokion is sung by the choir as the opening proclamation of the Great Doxology); after which we sing the Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"** (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου*).

| *Unto the upright light has dawned in darkness, merciful, compassionate, and righteous.* | |
| ***"Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."*** **"O Only-begotten Son"** (*Ὁ Μονογενής*). | |[^202]

Εἰσοδικὸν *Ἐκ γαστρὸς πρὸ Ἑωσφόρου ἐγέννησά σε*, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον *Ἡ γέννησίς σου*, τὸ Κοντάκιον *Ἡ παρθένος σήμερον τὸν Ὑπερούσιον τίκτει*, ἀντὶ τοῦ Τρισαγίου τὸ *Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε*, ὁ Ἀπόστολος καὶ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως *Μεγάλυνον ἡ ψυχή μου . . . Μυστήριον ξένον*. Κοινωνικὸν *Λύτρωσιν ἀπέστειλε Κύριος τῷ λαῷ αὐτοῦ, Ἀλληλούϊα*, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον *Ἡ γέννησίς σου* καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

*Σημείωσις.* Καθ’ ὅλον τὸ δωδεκαήμερον γίνεται ἐν τῇ τραπέζῃ κατάλυσις εἰς πάντα, ἐκτὸς τῆς Παραμονῆς τῶν Φώτων, ἥτις, ἂν ᾖ Σάββατον ἢ Κυριακή, ἐπιτρέπει κατάλυσιν οἴνου καὶ ἐλαίου.

# December 25: Liturgy Concluded / December 26: Synaxis of the Theotokos

## Divine Liturgy (Concluded) [Violakis, p. 273]

### Antiphon Three (Tone 4)

| Verses [Psalm 109 LXX] | Refrain |
| :--- | :--- |
| *The Lord said unto my Lord: Sit Thou at My right hand, until I make Thine enemies the footstool of Thy feet.* | *Thy Nativity, O Christ our God, etc.* |
| *A rod of power shall the Lord send forth unto Thee out of Zion.* | |
| *With Thee is dominion in the day of Thy power, in the brightness of Thy saints.* | |

Introit (Entrance Hymn): **"From the womb before the morning star have I begotten Thee"** (*Ἐκ γαστρὸς πρὸ Ἑωσφόρου ἐγέννησά σε*, Ps. 109:3 LXX). The Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"** (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου, Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*), the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin gives birth unto Him Who is transcendent in essence"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον τὸν Ὑπερούσιον τίκτει*); instead of the Trisagion: **"As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia"** (*Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε*, Gal. 3:27). The Epistle [Galatians 4:4–7] and the Holy Gospel [Matthew 2:1–12]. At the Megalynarion: **"Magnify, O my soul... A strange and most glorious mystery do I behold"** (*Μυστήριον ξένον*). Communion Verse: **"The Lord hath sent redemption unto His people. Alleluia"** (*Λύτρωσιν ἀπέστειλε Κύριος τῷ λαῷ αὐτοῦ*, Ps. 110:9 LXX), the Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"**, and Dismissal.

*Note.* Throughout the entire Twelve Days [Dodekahemeron] of the feast, there is general dispensation from fasting in the refectory, except on the Paramony [Eve] of Theophany, on which, if it falls on a Saturday or Sunday, wine and oil are permitted.

### The 26th Day. The Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos [Violakis, p. 273]

9. Both now and ever..."**: **"Glory to God in the highest"** (*Δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις Θεῷ*). Entrance with the censer: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Great Prokeimenon in Tone 7: **"Who is so great a God as our God? Thou art the God Who doest wonders"** (*Τίς Θεὸς μέγας ὡς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν; Σὺ εἶ ὁ Θεὸς ὁ ποιῶν θαυμάσια*, Ps. 76:14 LXX) with its verses. At the Aposticha: the Idiomela: **"A marvelous mystery"** (*Παράδοξον μυστήριον*) and the other two; **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**: **"In Bethlehem the shepherds hastened"** (*Ἐν Βηθλεὲμ συνέδραμον ποιμένες*). The Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"** (thrice), and Dismissal.
10.    On Saturday at Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"**, and the Hexapsalmos. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"** (thrice); then the daily Psalter (without the Polyeleos); the two Kathismata: **"Come, let us see, ye faithful"** (*Δεῦτε ἴδωμεν, πιστοί*) and **"Why art thou filled with wonder, O Mary?"** (*Τί θαυμάζεις, Μαριάμ;*); and Psalm 50 [LXX] recited plain; both Canons without verses, as yesterday. # December 26: Matins Concluded & Liturgy / Sunday after Nativity & St. Stephen

## Ὄρθρος καὶ Θεία Λειτουργία τῆς Συνάξεως (Συνέχεια) [Violakis, p. 274]

ψαλμὸς χῦμα· οἱ Κανόνες ἀμφότεροι ἄνευ Στίχων ὡς χθές, ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς ἡ Ὑπακοὴ, ἀφ’ ς΄ Κοντάκιον *Ὁ πρὸ Ἑωσφόρου Πατρὸς ἐκλάμψας*, ὁ Οἶκος καὶ τὸ Μηνολόγιον, αἱ Καταβασίαι *Ἔσωσε λαὸν* καὶ ψάλλεται ἡ Θ΄ Ὠδὴ καὶ τῶν δύο Κανόνων μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων καὶ ἡ Καταβασία *Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς*, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον *Ἐπεσκέψατο ἡμᾶς* ἐκ τρίτου. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους τὰ δ΄ Ἰδιόμελα *Εὐφραίνεσθε δίκαιοι*, *Δόξα*, *Σήμερον ἡ ἀόρατος φύσις* *Καὶ νῦν* *Σήμερον ὁ Χριστὸς*, (μέχρι τοῦ *ἡμεῖς δὲ ἀκαταπαύστως βοῶμεν*, καὶ ἄρχεται εὐθὺς ἡ) Δοξολογία Μ. καὶ τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον *Ἡ γέννησίς σου*.
11.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Ἀντίφωνα τῆς ἑορτῆς ὡς χθές, Εἰσοδικὸν *Ἐκ γαστρὸς πρὸ Ἑωσφόρου*, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον *Ἡ γέννησίς σου* καὶ τὸ Κοντάκιον *Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*· ἀντὶ τοῦ Τρισαγίου *Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε*, ὁ Ἀπόστολος τοῦ Σαββάτου μετὰ τὴν Χριστοῦ Γέννησιν *Τέκνον Τῖτε, δίωκε δικαιοσύνην* (τὸ ὀρθότερον εἶναι *Τέκνον Τιμόθεε*, Πρὸς Τιμόθεον, 6:11-16) καὶ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον ὡσαύτως *Τῷ καιρῷ ἐκείνῳ ἠκολούθησαν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ὄχλοι πολλοί*. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως, *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου . . . Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς*, Κοινωνικὸν *Λύτρωσιν ἀπέστειλε*, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον *Ἡ γέννησίς σου Χριστὲ* καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

---
⁵ Ἐν ἄλλαις ἡμέραις (ἐκτὸς δηλονότι τῆς συμπτώσεως τῆς ἑορτῆς ταύτης ἐν Σαββάτῳ ἢ Κυριακῇ), Ἀπόστολος λέγεται *Ἀδελφοί, ὁ ἁγιάζων καὶ οἱ ἁγιαζόμενοι* καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον *Ἀναχωρησάντων τῶν Μάγων*.

### Κυριακὴ μετὰ τὴν Χριστοῦ Γέννησιν, καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου Πρωτομάρτυρος καὶ Ἀρχιδιακόνου Στεφάνου [Violakis, p. 274]

12.    Τῷ αὐτῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ *Κύριε ἐκέκραξα* ψάλλομεν ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ δ΄, τῶν Θεοπατόρων τὸν Θεοπάτορα πάντες γ΄ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου Στεφάνου γ΄, *Δόξα* *Μνήμην ἐπιτελοῦμεν*, *Καὶ νῦν* τὸ α΄ Θεοτοκίον τοῦ ἤχου, Εἴσοδος, *Φῶς ἱλαρὸν*, καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ, *Δόξα* τοῦ Ἁγίου *Πρῶτος ἐν Μάρτυσιν ἐδείχθης*, *Καὶ νῦν* *Χορεύουσιν Ἄγγελοι*, Ἀπολυτίκια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τοῦ Ἁγίου, τὸ *Εὐαγγελίζου Ἰωσὴφ* καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

# December 26: Matins Concluded & Liturgy / Sunday after Nativity & St. Stephen

## Matins and the Divine Liturgy of the Synaxis (Concluded) [Violakis, p. 275]

Hypakoe recited plain; after the Sixth Ode, the Kontakion: **"He Who was begotten of the Father before the morning star"** (*Ὁ πρὸ Ἑωσφόρου Πατρὸς ἐκλάμψας*), the Ikos, and the Synaxarion of the Feast. The Katavasiai: **"He saved the people"** (*Ἔσωσε λαόν*); then the Ninth Ode of both Canons with their Megalynaria, and the Katavasia: **"Easier for us would it be"** (*Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς*). The Exapostilarion: **"Our Savior, the Dayspring from on high, hath visited us"** (*Ἐπεσκέψατο ἡμᾶς*) thrice. At the Praises: the 4 Idiomela: **"Be glad, O ye righteous"** (*Εὐφραίνεσθε, δίκαιοι*); **"Glory"**: **"Today the invisible nature"** (*Σήμερον ἡ ἀόρατος φύσις*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Today Christ is born in Bethlehem of the Virgin"** (*Σήμερον ὁ Χριστὸς*) up to the cue words **"and we cry aloud without ceasing: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will among men."** (Note: the concluding phrase of the above Theotokion is sung by the choir as the opening proclamation of the Great Doxology); after which we sing the Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"** (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου*).
11.    In the Divine Liturgy: the Antiphons of the Feast as yesterday. Introit (Entrance Hymn): **"From the womb before the morning star have I begotten Thee"** (*Ἐκ γαστρὸς πρὸ Ἑωσφόρου ἐγέννησά σε*, Ps. 109:3 LXX). The Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"**, and the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin gives birth unto Him Who is transcendent in essence"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*). Instead of the Trisagion: **"As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia"** (*Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε*, Gal. 3:27). The Epistle of the Saturday after the Nativity of Christ: **"O my son Timothy, follow after righteousness"** (*Τέκνον Τιμόθεε, δίωκε δικαιοσύνην*, 1 Tim. 6:11–16; note: the Greek text has "Titus", which is a typographical error for 1 Timothy 6:11–16); and the Holy Gospel likewise: **"At that time, great multitudes followed Jesus"** (*Τῷ καιρῷ ἐκείνῳ ἠκολούθησαν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ὄχλοι πολλοί*, Matt. 12:15–21). At the Megalynarion: **"Magnify, O my soul... Easier for us would it be"** (*Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς*). Communion Verse: **"The Lord hath sent redemption unto His people. Alleluia"** (*Λύτρωσιν ἀπέστειλε Κύριος τῷ λαῷ αὐτοῦ*, Ps. 110:9 LXX); the Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"**, and Dismissal.

*Note.* On other days (that is, outside the occurrence of this Feast on a Saturday or Sunday), the Epistle read is: **"Brethren, both He that sanctifieth and they who are sanctified are all of one"** (*Ἀδελφοί, ὁ ἁγιάζων καὶ οἱ ἁγιαζόμενοι*, Heb. 2:11–18); and the Holy Gospel: **"When the wise men had departed"** (*Ἀναχωρησάντων τῶν Μάγων*, Matt. 2:13–23).

### Sunday after the Nativity of Christ, and the Holy Protomartyr and Archdeacon Stephen [Violakis, p. 275]

12.    On that same Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm [Psalm 103 LXX] and the First Kathisma of the Psalter, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing 4 Resurrection Stichira, 3 of the Holy Forefathers [David, Joseph, and James]: **"Come, let us all praise the Ancestor of God"** (*Τὸν θεοπάτορα πάντες*), and 3 of Saint Stephen; **"Glory"**: **"Let us celebrate the memory"** (*Μνήμην ἐπιτελοῦμεν*); **"Both now and ever"**: the First Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance with the censer: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Prokeimenon. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; **"Glory"** of the Saint: **"Thou wast shown to be the first among martyrs"** (*Πρῶτος ἐν Μάρτυσιν ἐδείχθης*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"The Angels dance in chorus"** (*Χορεύουσιν Ἄγγελοι*). Dismissal Troparia: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of Saint Stephen, that of the Holy Forefathers: **"Proclaim the wonders, O Joseph"** (*Εὐαγγελίζου, Ἰωσήφ*), and Dismissal.[^204]

*(Printed Page 275)*

# December 27: Sunday after the Nativity / St. Stephen the Protomartyr & Apodosis of the Nativity

## Ὄρθρος καὶ Θεία Λειτουργία (Συνέχεια) [Violakis, p. 276]

13.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν, ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανὼν καὶ τὰ Τριαδικὰ *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*, εἶτα τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον *Ἡ γέννησίς σου Χριστὲ ὁ θεὸς* καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ *Θεὸς Κύριος* τὰ Ἀπολυτίκια ὡς εἰς τὸν Ἑσπερινὸν, εἶτα τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Πολυέλεος. Τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Καθίσματα καὶ ἀνὰ ἓν τῆς ἑορτῆς ἀντὶ τῶν Θεοτοκίων, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Κανόνες ὁ Ἀναστάσιμος καὶ ὁ τοῦ Μνήστορος *Χριστοῦ θεράπων μακάριε* μετὰ Στίχου *Ἅγιε τοῦ θεοῦ*, ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ Κάθισμα *Πατρὸς ὡς ἀληθῶς*, τὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου, καὶ τὸ *Χορὸς τῶν Προφητῶν*, ἀφ’ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον *Εὐφροσύνης σήμερον* καὶ ὁ Οἶκος, τὸ Μηνολόγιον τοῦ Ἁγίου καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς μετὰ τὴν Χριστοῦ Γέννησιν, αἱ Καταβασίαι *Ἔσωσε λαὸν* καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου. Εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν *Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*, Ἐξαποστειλάρια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τοῦ ἁγίου Στεφάνου, τὸ τοῦ Μνήστορος *Σὺν Ἰακώβῳ μέλψωμεν* καὶ τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους Ἀναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου δ΄, *Δόξα* *Αἷμα καὶ πῦρ*, *Καὶ νῦν* *Ὑπερευλογημένη*, Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ *Σήμερον σωτηρία*.

14.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Τυπικὰ καὶ οἱ Μακαρισμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου εἰς δ΄ καὶ ἐκ τῆς ς΄ Ὠδῆς τοῦ Κανόνος τοῦ Μνήστορος δ΄. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, *Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν . . . ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν*, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον, τὸ *Εὐαγγελίζου Ἰωσὴφ*, τὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου, καὶ τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ. Κοντάκιον *Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*, Ἀπόστολος τοῦ Ἁγίου καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον *Ἀναχωρησάντων τῶν Μάγων*. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*, Κοινωνικὸν *Αἰνεῖτε*, *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς* καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.
       Σημ. Τῆς μνήμης τοῦ ἁγίου Στεφάνου ἐν ἄλλαις ἡμέραις συμπιπτούσης (ἐκτὸς δηλονότι τῇ Κυριακῇ μετὰ τὴν Χριστοῦ Γέννησιν), ἡ Ἀκολουθία αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν μεθεόρτων ψάλλεται ὡς ἐστι διατεταγμένη ἐν τῷ Μηναίῳ· ἐν Σαββάτῳ δὲ συμπιπτούσης, Ἀπόστολος λέγεται τοῦ Ἁγίου, καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Σαββάτου μετὰ τὴν Χριστοῦ Γέννησιν.
